  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.

  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);

    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.

      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line ltx_leqno" lang="en-GB">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomology
<br class="ltx_break">as a Hecke module over a finite field</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Gabor Wiese
</span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">This article exhibits conditions under which
a certain parabolic group cohomology space
over a finite field <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔽</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}</annotation></semantics></math> is a faithful module for
the Hecke algebra of cuspidal Katz modular forms over
an algebraic closure of <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔽</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}</annotation></semantics></math>.
These results can e.g. be applied to compute cuspidal Katz
modular forms of weight one with
methods of linear algebra over <math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔽</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
    
<p id="abstract1.2" class="ltx_p">MSC Classif.: 11F25 (primary), 11F33, 11F67, 11Y40 (secondary).</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The space <math id="S1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C})</annotation></semantics></math> of holomorphic
modular cusp forms of weight <math id="S1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math> for the group
<math id="S1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> for some integer <math id="S1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> is related to
the parabolic group cohomology of <math id="S1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>
by the so-called Eichler-Shimura isomorphism (see e.g. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>,
Theorem 12.2.2)</p>
<table id="S1.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(1.1)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C})\oplus\overline{S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C})}\cong H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C}[X,Y]_{k-2})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C})\oplus\overline{S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C})}\cong H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C}[X,Y]_{k-2}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}[X,Y]_{k-2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}[X,Y]_{k-2}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the <math id="S1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℂ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}</annotation></semantics></math>-vector space of homogeneous
polynomials of degree <math id="S1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k-2</annotation></semantics></math> in two variables with the
standard <math id="S1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>SL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>-action.
For the definition of the parabolic group cohomology see
Section <a href="#S2" title="2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.
On the modular forms, as well as on the group cohomology
one disposes of natural Hecke operators, which are compatible
with the Eichler-Shimura isomorphism.
An immediate observation is
that <math id="S1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C}[X,Y]_{k-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C}[X,Y]_{k-2})</annotation></semantics></math>
is a free module of rank <math id="S1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> for
the complex Hecke algebra <math id="S1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{C}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>ℂ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{C}}</annotation></semantics></math> generated by the Hecke operators
in the endomorphism ring of <math id="S1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C})</annotation></semantics></math>.
This implies, in particular, that
<math id="S1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C}[X,Y]_{k-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C}[X,Y]_{k-2})</annotation></semantics></math> is a faithful <math id="S1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{C}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>ℂ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{C}}</annotation></semantics></math>-module.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In general there is no analogue of the Eichler-Shimura isomorphism
over finite fields. However, in the present article we show that the
above observation generalises to cuspidal Katz modular forms over finite fields
in certain cases.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Let now <math id="S1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the <math id="S1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-Hecke algebra generated
by the Hecke operators inside the endomorphism ring of the
cuspidal Katz modular forms <math id="S1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> of weight <math id="S1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>
for <math id="S1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> over the field <math id="S1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>.
In view of the observations from the Eichler-Shimura
isomorphism two questions arise naturally.</p>
<ol id="S1.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(a)</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Is <math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]_{k-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]_{k-2})</annotation></semantics></math> a faithful <math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math>-module?</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.0pt;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(b)</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Is <math id="S1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]_{k-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]_{k-2})</annotation></semantics></math> free of rank <math id="S1.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> as a <math id="S1.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math>-module?</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="S1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">A positive answer to Question (b) clearly implies a positive answer to (a).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Using <math id="S1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-adic Hodge theory (in particular the article <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>),
Edixhoven shows in Theorem 5.2 of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite> that
Question (a) has a positive answer in the
weight range <math id="S1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\leq k\leq p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\leq k\leq p-1</annotation></semantics></math>.
Emerton, Pollack and Weston were able to deduce from the fundamental work by
Wiles on Fermat’s last theorem
that Question (b) is true locally at primes of the Hecke algebra which
are <math id="S1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-ordinary and <math id="S1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-distinguished (see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>, Proposition 3.3.1)
for <math id="S1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-coefficients and the full
cohomology (i.e. not the parabolic subspace), from which the result follows
for <math id="S1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-coefficients and the full cohomology.
We should mention that a positive answer
to Question (a) with <math id="S1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-coefficients does not imply a positive answer over <math id="S1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The main result of the present article is to answer Question (a) positively
locally at <math id="S1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-ordinary primes of <math id="S1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math>
in the weight range <math id="S1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\leq k\leq p+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\leq k\leq p+1</annotation></semantics></math> (see Corollary <a href="#S6.Thmthm9" title="Corollary 6.9 ‣ Comparing Hecke algebras over 𝔽_𝑝 ‣ 6 Hecke algebras ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.9</span></a>).
A similar result for cuspidal modular forms for <math id="S1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> with a
Dirichlet character follows under certain rather weak assumptions
(see Theorem <a href="#S7.Thmthm4" title="Theorem 7.4 ‣ 7 Application to Γ_0⁢(𝑁) and characters ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.4</span></a>).
These results are obtained using techniques that were inspired
by the special case <math id="S1.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=2</annotation></semantics></math> of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, Theorem 5.2.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Let us point out the following consequence, which presented
the initial motivation for this study.
If the answer to Question (a) is yes, we may compute <math id="S1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> via
the Hecke operators on the finite dimensional <math id="S1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-vector space
<math id="S1.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]_{k-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]_{k-2})</annotation></semantics></math>.
This can be done explicitly on a computer and only requires
linear algebra methods.
The knowledge of the Hecke algebra is very interesting.
One can, for example,
try to verify whether it is a Gorenstein ring. This property is often implied
when the Hecke algebra is isomorphic to a deformation ring (as e.g. in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Techniques from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, Section 4, show how cuspidal Katz modular forms
of weight one over <math id="S1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}}</annotation></semantics></math> can be related to weight <math id="S1.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>.
We observe in Proposition <a href="#S8.Thmthm4" title="Proposition 8.4 ‣ 8 Application to weight one modular forms ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.4</span></a>
that the corresponding local factors of the Hecke algebra
in weight <math id="S1.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> are <math id="S1.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-ordinary.
Hence, a consequence of our result is that methods from <math id="S1.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-linear algebra
can be used for the computation of weight one Katz cusp forms (see Theorem <a href="#S8.Thmthm5" title="Theorem 8.5 ‣ 8 Application to weight one modular forms ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.5</span></a>).
The author carried out some such calculations and reported on them
in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">It should be mentioned that if one is not interested in the Hecke
algebra structure, but only in the systems of eigenvalues
of Hecke eigenforms in <math id="S1.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}})</annotation></semantics></math>, one can get them
directly from <math id="S1.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]_{k-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]_{k-2})</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S1.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>
(see e.g. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>, Proposition 4.3.1).
However, there may be more systems of eigenvalues in the group
cohomology than in <math id="S1.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}})</annotation></semantics></math>, but the extra ones can easily
be identified.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">This article is based on the use of group cohomology.
The author studied in his thesis <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite> and the article <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>
relations to modular symbols and a certain cohomology group on the corresponding
modular curve.
All these agree for instance for any congruence subgroup of <math id="S1.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>SL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>
if the characteristic of the base field is <math id="S1.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math> or in any characteristic for the
group <math id="S1.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S1.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">We add some remarks on Katz modular forms.
As a reference one can use <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>]</cite>
or <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>.
For <math id="S1.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=\mathbb{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ℂ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=\mathbb{C}</annotation></semantics></math>, the Katz cuspidal modular forms are precisely the holomorphic
cusp forms.
Under the assumptions <math id="S1.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>
one has <math id="S1.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{Z}[1/N])\otimes R\cong S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),R)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{Z}[1/N])\otimes R\cong S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),R)</annotation></semantics></math>
for any ring <math id="S1.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> in which <math id="S1.p10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> is invertible.
In particular, this means that any Katz cusp form over <math id="S1.p10.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}}</annotation></semantics></math> can be
lifted to characteristic zero in the same weight and level.
The previous statement does not hold for weight <math id="S1.p10.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=1</annotation></semantics></math> in general.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p11.1" class="ltx_p">Katz cusp forms over <math id="S1.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}}</annotation></semantics></math> for a prime <math id="S1.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> play an important
rôle in a modified version of Serre’s conjecture on modular forms
(see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>), as their use, on the one hand,
gets rid of some character lifting problems, and
on the other hand, allows one to minimise the weights of the modular forms.
In particular, odd, irreducible Galois representations
<math id="S1.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gal({\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}|\mathbb{Q})\to\mathrm{GL}_{2}({\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Gal</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ℚ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>ℚ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gal({\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}|\mathbb{Q})\to\mathrm{GL}_{2}({\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}})</annotation></semantics></math>
which are unramified at <math id="S1.p11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> are conjectured to correspond to
Katz eigenforms of weight one.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p12.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we should mention that William Stein has implemented <math id="S1.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-modular symbols
and the Hecke operators on them in Magma and Python. One could say that this article
is also about what they compute.</p>
</div>

and Theo van den Bogaart for sharing his insights in algebraic geometry.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">1.1 </span>Notation</h3>

<div id="S1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We denote by <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}</annotation></semantics></math> the semi-group of integral <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\times 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times 2</annotation></semantics></math>-matrices
with non-zero determinant. On it one has
Shimura’s main involution <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
c&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)}^{\iota}=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d&amp;-b\\
-c&amp;a\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">b</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">c</mi></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>ι</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi></mtd><mtd><mrow><mo mathsize="0.700em">−</mo><mi mathsize="0.700em">b</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mo mathsize="0.700em">−</mo><mi mathsize="0.700em">c</mi></mrow></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
c&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)}^{\iota}=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d&amp;-b\\
-c&amp;a\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.
For a ring <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> the notation <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R[X,Y]_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R[X,Y]_{n}</annotation></semantics></math> stands for the homogeneous polynomials
of degree <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> in the variables <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X,Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X,Y</annotation></semantics></math>.
We let</p>
<table id="S1.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{n}(R):=\Sym^{n}(R^{2})\cong R[X,Y]_{n}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>Sym</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{n}(R):=\Sym^{n}(R^{2})\cong R[X,Y]_{n}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">which we equip with the natural left <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}</annotation></semantics></math>-semi-group action.
If <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> is an <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>-module, let <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V^{\vee}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>V</mi><mo>∨</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V^{\vee}</annotation></semantics></math> be the dual <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>-module <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\rm Hom}_{R}(V,R)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Hom</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\rm Hom}_{R}(V,R)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As usual, the upper half plane is denoted by <math id="S1.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℍ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{H}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Moreover, we shall use the standard congruence subgroups <math id="S1.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma(N)</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S1.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{0}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{0}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S1.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>SL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> for an integer <math id="S1.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>,
which are defined to consist of the matrices <math id="S1.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
c&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">b</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">c</mi></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>SL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
c&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>
reducing modulo <math id="S1.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S1.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;0\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;0\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S1.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;*\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mo mathsize="0.700em">∗</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;*\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> resp. <math id="S1.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}*&amp;*\\
0&amp;*\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mo mathsize="0.700em">∗</mo></mtd><mtd><mo mathsize="0.700em">∗</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mo mathsize="0.700em">∗</mo></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}*&amp;*\\
0&amp;*\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Parabolic group cohomology</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section we recall the definition of parabolic group
cohomology and present some properties to be used in the
sequel. We shall use standard facts on group cohomology
without special reference. The reader can
for example consult <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Cohomology of <math id="S2.SSx1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="S2.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The group <math id="S2.SSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> is freely generated by the matrix classes of
<math id="S2.SSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma:=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&amp;-1\\
1&amp;0\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mrow><mo mathsize="0.700em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma:=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&amp;-1\\
1&amp;0\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau:=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;-1\\
1&amp;0\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mrow><mo mathsize="0.700em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau:=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;-1\\
1&amp;0\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.
A consequence is the following special case of the
<span id="S2.SSx1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Mayer-Vietoris sequence</span> (see e.g. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>, p. 221).
For any ring <math id="S2.SSx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> and any left <math id="S2.SSx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R[\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R[\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})]</annotation></semantics></math>-module <math id="S2.SSx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>
the sequence</p>
<table id="S2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(2.2)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\to M^{\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})}\to M^{\langle\sigma\rangle}\oplus M^{\langle\tau\rangle}\to M\\
\to H^{1}(\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z}),M)\to H^{1}(\langle\sigma\rangle,M)\oplus H^{1}(\langle\tau\rangle,M)\to 0" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtable displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></msup><mo>⊕</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_right" columnalign="right"><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\to M^{\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})}\to M^{\langle\sigma\rangle}\oplus M^{\langle\tau\rangle}\to M\\

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SSx1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">is exact and for all <math id="S2.SSx1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math> one has isomorphisms</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{i}(\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z}),M)\cong H^{i}(\langle\sigma\rangle,M)\oplus H^{i}(\langle\tau\rangle,M)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{i}(\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z}),M)\cong H^{i}(\langle\sigma\rangle,M)\oplus H^{i}(\langle\tau\rangle,M).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</div>
<div id="S2.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 2.1</span></span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> be a ring and <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\leq\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\leq\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> be a subgroup of finite index such
that all the orders of all stabiliser groups <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{x}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathbb{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℍ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathbb{H}</annotation></semantics></math> are invertible in <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then for all <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R[\Gamma]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R[\Gamma]</annotation></semantics></math>-modules <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> one has
<math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Gamma,V)=M/(M^{\langle\sigma\rangle}+M^{\langle\tau\rangle})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Gamma,V)=M/(M^{\langle\sigma\rangle}+M^{\langle\tau\rangle})</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M={\rm Coind}_{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})}(V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>Coind</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M={\rm Coind}_{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})}(V)</annotation></semantics></math>
and
<math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{i}(\Gamma,V)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{i}(\Gamma,V)=0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.SSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SSx1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>We first recall that any non-trivially stabilised point <math id="S2.SSx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S2.SSx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℍ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{H}</annotation></semantics></math>
is conjugate by an element of <math id="S2.SSx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> to either <math id="S2.SSx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S2.SSx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\zeta_{3}=e^{2\pi i/3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\zeta_{3}=e^{2\pi i/3}</annotation></semantics></math>,
whence all non-trivial stabiliser groups are of the form
<math id="S2.SSx1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\langle\sigma\rangle g^{-1}\cap\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>∩</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\langle\sigma\rangle g^{-1}\cap\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math>
or <math id="S2.SSx1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\langle\tau\rangle g^{-1}\cap\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>∩</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\langle\tau\rangle g^{-1}\cap\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="S2.SSx1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>.
From Mackey’s formula (see e.g. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>) one obtains</p>
<table id="S2.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

g^{-1}\cap\Gamma,V)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SSx1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">for all <math id="S2.SSx1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> and a similar result for <math id="S2.SSx1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>.
Due to the invertibility assumption the result follows from Shapiro’s lemma
and Equations (<a href="#S2.E2" title="In Cohomology of PSL_2⁢(ℤ) ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>) and (<a href="#S2.E3" title="In Cohomology of PSL_2⁢(ℤ) ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>).
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SSx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SSx1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The assumptions of the proposition are for instance always satisfied
if <math id="S2.SSx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> is a field of characteristic not <math id="S2.SSx1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S2.SSx1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>. They also
hold for <math id="S2.SSx1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S2.SSx1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 4</annotation></semantics></math> over any ring.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SSx2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Definition of parabolic group cohomology</h3>

<div id="S2.SSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S2.SSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> be a ring, <math id="S2.SSx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\leq\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\leq\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> a subgroup of finite index
and <math id="S2.SSx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=\tau\sigma=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;1\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=\tau\sigma=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;1\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.
One defines the <span id="S2.SSx2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">parabolic group cohomology group for the <math id="S2.SSx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R[\Gamma]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R[\Gamma]</annotation></semantics></math>-module <math id="S2.SSx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math></span>
as the kernel of the restriction map in</p>
