encoding="application/x-tex">\textstyle{(V_{k-2}(R))_{\Gamma}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}</annotation></semantics></math></span></span></foreignObject></g><path style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;" d="M 222.6265347381672 -54.22218188682631 L 223.18000629826736 -54.22218188682631" fill="none" stroke="#000000"></path><g transform="translate(222.91,0) translate(0,-53.73)"><path style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;" d="M 0 0 A 13.84 13.84 45 0 0 2.77 6.92" fill="none" stroke="#000000"></path><path style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;" d="M 0 0 A 13.84 13.84 45 0 1 -2.77 6.92" fill="none" stroke="#000000"></path></g><path style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;" d="M 222.6265347381672 -53.725358079673015 L 223.18000629826736 -53.725358079673015" fill="none" stroke="#000000"></path><g transform="translate(75.05,0) translate(0,-63.34) translate(4.15,0) translate(0,-3.46)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:0.5em;--ltx-fo-height:0.64em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="8.92" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 8.92)" width="6.92"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><math id="S2.Ex9.m1.pic1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textstyle{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textstyle{0}</annotation></semantics></math></span></span></foreignObject></g><g transform="translate(215.3,0) translate(0,-63.34) translate(4.15,0) translate(0,-3.46)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:0.5em;--ltx-fo-height:0.64em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="8.92" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 8.92)" width="6.92"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><math id="S2.Ex9.m1.pic1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textstyle{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textstyle{0}</annotation></semantics></math></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SSx4.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where the products are taken over
<math id="S2.SSx4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\Gamma\backslash\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})/\langle T\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">\</mo><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\Gamma\backslash\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})/\langle T\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>,
and <math id="S2.SSx4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{g}=\Gamma\cap\langle gTg^{-1}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>∩</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{g}=\Gamma\cap\langle gTg^{-1}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>.
The exactness of the first row is the contents of Parts (a) and (b).
That the columns are exact follows from Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 2.2 ‣ Definition of parabolic group cohomology ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>.
The zero on the right of the second row is due to the fact that
<math id="S2.SSx4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> is free on one generator.
That generator is of the form <math id="S2.SSx4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;r\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)g^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">r</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;r\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)g^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S2.SSx4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\mid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\mid N</annotation></semantics></math>,
so that <math id="S2.SSx4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is invertible in <math id="S2.SSx4.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>. The zero on the left is
trivial for <math id="S2.SSx4.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=2</annotation></semantics></math> and for <math id="S2.SSx4.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\leq k\leq p+2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\leq k\leq p+2</annotation></semantics></math> it is
a consequence of Lemma <a href="#S2.Thmthm4" title="Lemma 2.4 ‣ The module 𝑉_𝑛⁢(𝑅) ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.4</span></a>.
Part (c) now follows from the snake lemma
and Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm5" title="Proposition 2.5 ‣ The module 𝑉_𝑛⁢(𝑅) ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a>, which implies that the bottom
map is an injection.
∎</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Hecke action</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Hecke operators conceptually come from Hecke correspondences
on modular curves respectively modular stacks. They are best described on
the moduli interpretations (see e.g. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>, 3.2 and 7.3).
All Hecke operators that we will encounter in this article
arise like this.
This section presents Hecke operators on group
cohomology and the principal result is the behaviour of the Hecke
operators with respect to Shapiro’s lemma. That result
was obtained by Ash and Stevens (<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>, Lemma 2.2). Here, however,
we avoid their rather heavy language of weakly compatible Hecke
pairs. Instead, the description of Hecke operators
on group cohomology is used which comes directly from
the Hecke correspondences (formally one has to work on the modular stacks
with locally constant coefficients, in case of non-trivially
stabilised points). For the description we follow <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>, 12.4.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Hecke operators on group cohomology</h3>

<div id="S3.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.SSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> be a ring, <math id="S3.SSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\in\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\in\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\leq\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\leq\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>
be a subgroup containing some <math id="S3.SSx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma(N)</annotation></semantics></math>.
We use the notations <math id="S3.SSx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{\alpha}:=\Gamma\cap\alpha^{-1}\Gamma\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>∩</mo><mrow><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{\alpha}:=\Gamma\cap\alpha^{-1}\Gamma\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="S3.SSx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma^{\alpha}:=\Gamma\cap\alpha\Gamma\alpha^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>α</mi></msup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>∩</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma^{\alpha}:=\Gamma\cap\alpha\Gamma\alpha^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>,
where we consider <math id="S3.SSx1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> as an element of <math id="S3.SSx1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GL}_{2}(\mathbb{Q})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℚ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GL}_{2}(\mathbb{Q})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Both groups are commensurable with <math id="S3.SSx1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Suppose that <math id="S3.SSx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> is an <math id="S3.SSx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>-module with a <math id="S3.SSx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}</annotation></semantics></math>-semi-group action
which restricts to an action by <math id="S3.SSx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math>.
The <span id="S3.SSx1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Hecke operator</span> <math id="S3.SSx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> acting on group
cohomology is the composite</p>
<table id="S3.Ex10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Gamma,V)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}}H^{1}(\Gamma^{\alpha},V)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{conj}_{\alpha}}H^{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},V)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{cores}}H^{1}(\Gamma,V)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">res</mo></mover><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>α</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.700em">conj</mi><mi mathsize="0.710em">α</mi></msub></mover><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">cores</mo></mover><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Gamma,V)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}}H^{1}(\Gamma^{\alpha},V)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{conj}_{\alpha}}H^{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},V)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{cores}}H^{1}(\Gamma,V).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SSx1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">The first map is the usual <span id="S3.SSx1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">restriction</span>, and the third one is the
so-called <span id="S3.SSx1.p2.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">corestriction</span>, which one also finds in the
literature under the name <span id="S3.SSx1.p2.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">transfer</span>.
We explicitly describe the second map on non-homogeneous cocycles
(cf. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>, p. 116):</p>
<table id="S3.Ex11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{conj}_{\alpha}:H^{1}(\Gamma^{\alpha},V)\to H^{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},V),\;\;c\mapsto\big(g_{\alpha}\mapsto\alpha^{\iota}.c(\alpha g_{\alpha}\alpha^{-1})\big)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>conj</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>α</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.727em">,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mi>ι</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>c</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><msup><mi>α</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{conj}_{\alpha}:H^{1}(\Gamma^{\alpha},V)\to H^{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},V),\;\;c\mapsto\big(g_{\alpha}\mapsto\alpha^{\iota}.c(\alpha g_{\alpha}\alpha^{-1})\big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S3.SSx1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">There is a similar description on the parabolic subspace
and the two are compatible.
The following formula can also be found in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>, p. 116,
and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite>, Section 8.3.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 3.1</span></span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Suppose that <math id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\alpha\Gamma=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}\Gamma\delta_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>⋃</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\alpha\Gamma=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}\Gamma\delta_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is a disjoint
union. Then the Hecke operator <math id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> acts on <math id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Gamma,V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Gamma,V)</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma,V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma,V)</annotation></semantics></math> by
sending the non-homogeneous cocyle <math id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\alpha}c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\alpha}c</annotation></semantics></math> defined by</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(T_{\alpha}c)(g)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\delta_{i}^{\iota}c(\delta_{i}g\delta_{j(i)}^{-1})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><mrow><msubsup><mi>δ</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>ι</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>δ</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(T_{\alpha}c)(g)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\delta_{i}^{\iota}c(\delta_{i}g\delta_{j(i)}^{-1})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">for <math id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math>. Here <math id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j(i)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j(i)</annotation></semantics></math> is the index such that <math id="S3.Thmthm1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{i}g\delta_{j(i)}^{-1}\in\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>δ</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{i}g\delta_{j(i)}^{-1}\in\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SSx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SSx1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>We only have to describe the corestriction explicitly. For that we notice that one has
<math id="S3.SSx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}\Gamma_{\alpha}g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>⋃</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}\Gamma_{\alpha}g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>
with <math id="S3.SSx1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha g_{i}=\delta_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha g_{i}=\delta_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. Furthermore the corestriction of a non-homogeneous
cocycle <math id="S3.SSx1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u\in H^{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u\in H^{1}(\Gamma_{\alpha},V)</annotation></semantics></math> is the cocycle <math id="S3.SSx1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{cores}(u)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>cores</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{cores}(u)</annotation></semantics></math> uniquely
given by</p>
<table id="S3.Ex13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{cores}(u)(g)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}g_{i}^{-1}u(g_{i}gg_{j(i)}^{-1})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>cores</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{cores}(u)(g)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}g_{i}^{-1}u(g_{i}gg_{j(i)}^{-1})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SSx1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">for <math id="S3.SSx1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math>. Combining with the explicit description of the map <math id="S3.SSx1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{conj}_{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>conj</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{conj}_{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math>
yields the result.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SSx1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Suppose now that <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma=\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma=\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> (resp. <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma=\Gamma_{0}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma=\Gamma_{0}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>).
For a positive integer <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>, the <span id="S3.SSx1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Hecke operator</span> <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{n}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{\alpha}T_{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>α</mi></msub><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{\alpha}T_{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math>,
where the sum runs through a system of representatives of the double
cosets <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\backslash\Delta^{n}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">\</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\backslash\Delta^{n}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> for
the set <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta^{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta^{n}</annotation></semantics></math> of matrices <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
c&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\in\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">b</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">c</mi></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
c&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\in\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}</annotation></semantics></math> of
determinant <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
c&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\equiv\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;*\\
0&amp;*\end{smallmatrix}\right)\,\mathrm{mod}\,N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">b</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">c</mi></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mo mathsize="0.700em">∗</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mo mathsize="0.700em">∗</mo></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>mod</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
c&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\equiv\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;*\\
0&amp;*\end{smallmatrix}\right)\,\mathrm{mod}\,N</annotation></semantics></math>
(resp. <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
c&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\equiv\left(\begin{smallmatrix}*&amp;*\\
0&amp;*\end{smallmatrix}\right)\,\mathrm{mod}\,N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">b</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">c</mi></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mo mathsize="0.700em">∗</mo></mtd><mtd><mo mathsize="0.700em">∗</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mo mathsize="0.700em">∗</mo></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>mod</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
c&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\equiv\left(\begin{smallmatrix}*&amp;*\\
0&amp;*\end{smallmatrix}\right)\,\mathrm{mod}\,N</annotation></semantics></math>).
For a prime <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> one has <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{p}=T_{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{p}=T_{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;0\\
0&amp;p\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">p</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;0\\
0&amp;p\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.
If <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma=\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma=\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>
and the integer <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> is coprime to <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>,
the <span id="S3.SSx1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">diamond operator</span>
<math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle d\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle d\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> for any matrix <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>SL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> whose reduction
modulo <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d^{-1}&amp;0\\
0&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msup><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi><mrow><mo mathsize="0.700em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mrow></msup></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d^{-1}&amp;0\\
0&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.
The diamond operator gives a group action by <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>
(with <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> acting trivially).
If the level is <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="NM" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">NM</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N,M)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N,M)=1</annotation></semantics></math>, then we can separate the
diamond operator into two parts
<math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle d\rangle=\langle d\rangle_{M}\times\langle d\rangle_{N}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>d</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>M</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>N</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle d\rangle=\langle d\rangle_{M}\times\langle d\rangle_{N},</annotation></semantics></math>
corresponding to <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/NM\mathbb{Z}\cong\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/NM\mathbb{Z}\cong\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The Hecke and diamond operators satisfy the “usual” Euler product
and one has the formulae
<math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{n}T_{m}=T_{nm}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{n}T_{m}=T_{nm}</annotation></semantics></math> for any pair
of coprime integers <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n,m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n,m</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{p^{r+1}}=T_{p^{r}}T_{p}-p^{k-1}\langle p\rangle T_{p^{r-1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><msup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><msup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{p^{r+1}}=T_{p^{r}}T_{p}-p^{k-1}\langle p\rangle T_{p^{r-1}}</annotation></semantics></math>
if <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{p^{r+1}}=T_{p^{r}}T_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><msup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{p^{r+1}}=T_{p^{r}}T_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> if <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\mid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\mid N</annotation></semantics></math>
for the action on <math id="S3.SSx1.p4.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SSx2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Hecke operators and Shapiro’s lemma</h3>

<div id="S3.SSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.SSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N,M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N,M</annotation></semantics></math> be coprime positive integers.
In order to test compatibility of the Hecke operators
with Shapiro’s lemma we need to extend the <math id="S3.SSx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>-action on
<math id="S3.SSx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\rm Coind}_{\Gamma_{1}(NM)}^{\Gamma_{1}(N)}(V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>Coind</mi><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\rm Coind}_{\Gamma_{1}(NM)}^{\Gamma_{1}(N)}(V)</annotation></semantics></math> to a <math id="S3.SSx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}</annotation></semantics></math>-semi-group action
“in the right way”. For that we define the <math id="S3.SSx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>-module <math id="S3.SSx2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}(M,V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}(M,V)</annotation></semantics></math> as</p>
<table id="S3.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{f\in{\rm Hom}_{R}(R[(\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z})^{2}],V)\;|\;f((u,v))=0\;\forall(u,v)\text{ s.t. }\langle u,v\rangle\neq\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Hom</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.447em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> s.t. </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{f\in{\rm Hom}_{R}(R[(\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z})^{2}],V)\;|\;f((u,v))=0\;\forall(u,v)\text{ s.t. }\langle u,v\rangle\neq\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SSx2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">It carries the left <math id="S3.SSx2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}</annotation></semantics></math>-semi-group action
<math id="S3.SSx2.p1.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(g.f)((u,v))=gf((u,v)g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(g.f)((u,v))=gf((u,v)g)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S3.SSx2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f\in\mathcal{W}(M,V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f\in\mathcal{W}(M,V)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SSx2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S3.SSx2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(u,v)\in(\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z})^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(u,v)\in(\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z})^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmthm2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmthm2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.2</span></span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmthm2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmthm2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmthm2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The homomorphism</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{W}(M,V)\to{\rm Hom}_{R[\Gamma_{1}(NM)]}(R[\Gamma_{1}(N)],V),\;\;\;f\mapsto\big(g\mapsto(g.f)((0,1))\big)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>Hom</mi><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="1.007em">,</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}(M,V)\to{\rm Hom}_{R[\Gamma_{1}(NM)]}(R[\Gamma_{1}(N)],V),\;\;\;f\mapsto\big(g\mapsto(g.f)((0,1))\big)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.Thmthm2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmthm2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">is an isomorphism of left <math id="S3.Thmthm2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>-modules (for the restricted action on <math id="S3.Thmthm2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}(M,V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}(M,V)</annotation></semantics></math>).
In particular, <math id="S3.Thmthm2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}(M,V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}(M,V)</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to <math id="S3.Thmthm2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\rm Coind}_{\Gamma_{1}(NM)}^{\Gamma_{1}(N)}(V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>Coind</mi><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\rm Coind}_{\Gamma_{1}(NM)}^{\Gamma_{1}(N)}(V)</annotation></semantics></math>
as a left <math id="S3.Thmthm2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>-module.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SSx2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>As <math id="S3.SSx2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SSx2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> are coprime, reduction modulo <math id="S3.SSx2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> defines a surjection from
<math id="S3.SSx2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> onto <math id="S3.SSx2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>SL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>. This implies that the map</p>
<table id="S3.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(NM)\backslash\Gamma_{1}(N)\xrightarrow{A\mapsto(0,1)A\text{ mod }M}(\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z})^{2}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">\</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.700em">A</mi><mo mathsize="0.700em" stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="0.700em" minsize="0.700em">(</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn><mo maxsize="0.700em" minsize="0.700em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.700em">A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext mathsize="0.700em"> mod </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.700em">M</mi></mrow></mrow></mover><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(NM)\backslash\Gamma_{1}(N)\xrightarrow{A\mapsto(0,1)A\text{ mod }M}(\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z})^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SSx2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">is injective, and its image is the set of the <math id="S3.SSx2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(u,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(u,v)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S3.SSx2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}=\langle u,v\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}=\langle u,v\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>.
As the <math id="S3.SSx2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(NM)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(NM)</annotation></semantics></math>-action on <math id="S3.SSx2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> is the restriction of a <math id="S3.SSx2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>-action,
the coinduced module can be identified with
<math id="S3.SSx2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\rm Hom}_{R}(R[\Gamma_{1}(NM)\backslash\Gamma_{1}(N)],V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Hom</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">\</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\rm Hom}_{R}(R[\Gamma_{1}(NM)\backslash\Gamma_{1}(N)],V)</annotation></semantics></math>.
From this the claimed isomorphism follows directly.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmthm3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmthm3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.3</span></span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmthm3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N,n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N,n</annotation></semantics></math> be positive integers.
We set</span></p>

c&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\in\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}|\det\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
c&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)=n,\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\

</table>
<p id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There is the decomposition</span></p>

0&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> runs through the integers such that <math id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,N)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,N)=1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="ad=n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">ad=n</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> through a system
of representatives of <math id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>. Here <math id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{a}\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>SL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{a}\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> is a matrix reducing
to <math id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a^{-1}&amp;0\\
0&amp;a\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msup><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi><mrow><mo mathsize="0.700em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mrow></msup></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a^{-1}&amp;0\\
0&amp;a\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.Thmthm3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SSx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SSx2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>This is <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite>, Proposition 3.36.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SSx2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The Shapiro map is the isomorphism on cohomology groups</p>
<table id="S3.Ex19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Sh}:H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathcal{W}(M,V))\to H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(NM),V)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Sh</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Sh}:H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathcal{W}(M,V))\to H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(NM),V)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SSx2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">which is induced by the homomorphism <math id="S3.SSx2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}(M,V)\to V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}(M,V)\to V</annotation></semantics></math>,
sending <math id="S3.SSx2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SSx2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f((0,1))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>,</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f((0,1))</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmthm4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmthm4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 3.4</span></span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmthm4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmthm4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmthm4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For all integers <math id="S3.Thmthm4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n,d\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n,d\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S3.Thmthm4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(d,N)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(d,N)=1</annotation></semantics></math> we have</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{n}\circ\mathrm{Sh}=\mathrm{Sh}\circ T_{n}\;\;\;\text{ and }\;\;\;\langle d\rangle_{N}\circ\mathrm{Sh}=\mathrm{Sh}\circ\langle d\rangle_{N}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>Sh</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Sh</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic"> and </mtext><mo lspace="0.840em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>d</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>N</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>Sh</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Sh</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>N</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{n}\circ\mathrm{Sh}=\mathrm{Sh}\circ T_{n}\;\;\;\text{ and }\;\;\;\langle d\rangle_{N}\circ\mathrm{Sh}=\mathrm{Sh}\circ\langle d\rangle_{N}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
