<div id="S3.SSx2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SSx2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>We first prove the statement for <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For every integer <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> dividing <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,N)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,N)=1</annotation></semantics></math>
we choose a matrix <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> such that it reduces to
<math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a^{-1}&amp;0\\
0&amp;a\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msup><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi><mrow><mo mathsize="0.700em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mrow></msup></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a^{-1}&amp;0\\
0&amp;a\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>.
If <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,M)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,M)=1</annotation></semantics></math>, then we also impose that <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>
reduces to <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a^{-1}&amp;0\\
0&amp;a\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msup><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi><mrow><mo mathsize="0.700em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mrow></msup></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a^{-1}&amp;0\\
0&amp;a\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>.
If <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,M)\neq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,M)\neq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, then we want <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{a}\equiv\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;0\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{a}\equiv\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;0\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>.
A simple calculation shows that <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,1)\big(\sigma_{a}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
0&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\big)^{\iota}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">a</mi></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">b</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mi>ι</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,1)\big(\sigma_{a}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&amp;b\\
0&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\big)^{\iota}</annotation></semantics></math>
is congruent to <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> if <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,M)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,M)=1</annotation></semantics></math> respectively to <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,a)</annotation></semantics></math> if <math id="S3.SSx2.p5.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,M)\neq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,M)\neq 1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SSx2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">A set of explicit coset representatives of
<math id="S3.SSx2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(NM)\backslash\Delta_{1}(NM)^{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">\</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(NM)\backslash\Delta_{1}(NM)^{n}</annotation></semantics></math>
is given by Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmthm3" title="Lemma 3.3 ‣ Hecke operators and Shapiro’s lemma ‣ 3 Hecke action ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> as a subset
of coset representatives of
<math id="S3.SSx2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)\backslash\Delta_{1}(N)^{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo rspace="0.222em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">\</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)\backslash\Delta_{1}(N)^{n}</annotation></semantics></math>,
namely of those with <math id="S3.SSx2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,M)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,M)=1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SSx2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx2.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Let now <math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\in H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathcal{W}(M,V))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c\in H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathcal{W}(M,V))</annotation></semantics></math> be a cocycle.
Then by Proposition <a href="#S3.Thmthm1" title="Proposition 3.1 ‣ Hecke operators on group cohomology ‣ 3 Hecke action ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> and the definition of the <math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}</annotation></semantics></math>-action on
<math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}(M,V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}(M,V)</annotation></semantics></math> we have for <math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\Gamma_{1}(NM)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\Gamma_{1}(NM)</annotation></semantics></math></p>

<p id="S3.SSx2.p7.2" class="ltx_p">where the sum runs over the above coset representatives for
<math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)\backslash\Delta_{1}(N)^{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo rspace="0.222em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">\</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)\backslash\Delta_{1}(N)^{n}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{\delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{\delta}</annotation></semantics></math>
is chosen among these representatives such that
<math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta g\widetilde{\delta}^{-1}\in\Gamma_{1}(NM)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>δ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta g\widetilde{\delta}^{-1}\in\Gamma_{1}(NM)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Moreover, we have</p>

<p id="S3.SSx2.p7.3" class="ltx_p">where now the sum only runs through the subset described above.
By what we have remarked right above <math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,1)\delta^{\iota}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>ι</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,1)\delta^{\iota}</annotation></semantics></math> is congruent
to <math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> if and only if
<math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,M)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,M)=1</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,M)\neq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,M)\neq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle a\rangle\neq\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle a\rangle\neq\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>,
but we have <math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,1)\delta^{\iota}\equiv(0,a)\,\mathrm{mod}\,N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>ι</mi></msup></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>mod</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,1)\delta^{\iota}\equiv(0,a)\,\mathrm{mod}\,N</annotation></semantics></math>.
This proves the compatibility for <math id="S3.SSx2.p7.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SSx2.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx2.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle d\rangle_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>N</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle d\rangle_{N}</annotation></semantics></math> only depends on <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>, we may suppose
that <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> is congruent to <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. We choose <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=\sigma_{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=\sigma_{d}</annotation></semantics></math>
such that it reduces to <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d^{-1}&amp;0\\
0&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msup><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi><mrow><mo mathsize="0.700em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mrow></msup></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d^{-1}&amp;0\\
0&amp;d\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>
and to <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;0\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;0\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>.
For <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\in H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathcal{W}(M,V))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c\in H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathcal{W}(M,V))</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SSx2.p8.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\Gamma_{1}(NM)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\Gamma_{1}(NM)</annotation></semantics></math>
the formula</p>

<p id="S3.SSx2.p8.2" class="ltx_p">follows.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmthm5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmthm5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 3.5</span></span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmthm5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmthm5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmthm5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="S3.Thmthm5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(n,M)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(n,M)=1</annotation></semantics></math> we define the <math id="S3.Thmthm5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R[\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R[\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}]</annotation></semantics></math>-isomorphism</span></p>

<p id="S3.Thmthm5.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmthm5.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Then we have</span></p>

<div id="S3.SSx2.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx2.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SSx2.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>Let <math id="S3.SSx2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>SL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> be a matrix
reducing to <math id="S3.SSx2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}n^{-1}&amp;0\\
0&amp;n\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msup><mi mathsize="0.700em">n</mi><mrow><mo mathsize="0.700em">−</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mrow></msup></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">n</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}n^{-1}&amp;0\\
0&amp;n\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.SSx2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>
and to <math id="S3.SSx2.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;0\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;0\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.SSx2.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>. This means in particular that
<math id="S3.SSx2.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\in\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\in\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence, for a cocycle <math id="S3.SSx2.p9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\in H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathcal{W}(M,V))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c\in H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathcal{W}(M,V))</annotation></semantics></math>
we have</p>
<table id="S3.Ex26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{-1}c(\sigma g\sigma^{-1})=c(g)+(g-1)c(\sigma^{-1})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{-1}c(\sigma g\sigma^{-1})=c(g)+(g-1)c(\sigma^{-1}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SSx2.p9.2" class="ltx_p">so that the equality <math id="S3.SSx2.p9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c(\sigma g\sigma^{-1})=\sigma c(g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c(\sigma g\sigma^{-1})=\sigma c(g)</annotation></semantics></math>
holds in <math id="S3.SSx2.p9.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathcal{W}(M,V))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathcal{W}(M,V))</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SSx2.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SSx2.p10.1" class="ltx_p">We can now check the claim.
First we have</p>
<table id="S3.Ex27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex27.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(\langle n\rangle_{M}\circ\mathrm{Sh})(c)(g)=\sigma^{\iota}\big((\sigma.c(g))((0,1))\big)=c(g)((0,1)\sigma)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>n</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>M</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>Sh</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mi>ι</mi></msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>c</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\langle n\rangle_{M}\circ\mathrm{Sh})(c)(g)=\sigma^{\iota}\big((\sigma.c(g))((0,1))\big)=c(g)((0,1)\sigma).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SSx2.p10.2" class="ltx_p">This agrees with <math id="S3.SSx2.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathrm{Sh}\circ{\rm mult}_{n})(c)(g)=c(g)((0,n))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Sh</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>mult</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathrm{Sh}\circ{\rm mult}_{n})(c)(g)=c(g)((0,n))</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Reduction to weight <math id="S4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> for parabolic group cohomology</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section deals with the reduction to weight <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> for parabolic group
cohomology, by which we mean that the parabolic group
cohomology over <math id="S4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math>
and weight <math id="S4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\leq k\leq p+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\leq k\leq p+1</annotation></semantics></math> is related to the weight two parabolic
group cohomology of <math id="S4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(Np)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(Np)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Hence, the parabolic group cohomology shows a
behaviour similar to that of modular forms (cf. Proposition <a href="#S5.Thmthm1" title="Proposition 5.1 (Serre) ‣ Reduction to weight 2 for modular forms ‣ 5 Modular forms of weight 2 and level 𝑁⁢𝑝 ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>).
Roughly speaking, the reduction to weight <math id="S4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> on group cohomology comes from the
decomposition of <math id="S4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\rm Coind}_{\Gamma_{1}(Np)}^{\Gamma_{1}(N)}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>Coind</mi><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\rm Coind}_{\Gamma_{1}(Np)}^{\Gamma_{1}(N)}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> into
simple <math id="S4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}[\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{F}_{p})]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>SL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}[\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{F}_{p})]</annotation></semantics></math>-modules. Those are precisely the
<math id="S4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\leq d\leq p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\leq d\leq p-1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The contents of this section is already partly present in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>.
However, in that paper the parabolic subspace is not treated.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Decomposition of <math id="S4.SSx1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="S4.SSx1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}[\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}[\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}]</annotation></semantics></math>-module</h3>

<div id="S4.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now relate the <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}[\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}[\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}]</annotation></semantics></math>-modules
<math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\leq d\leq p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\leq d\leq p-1</annotation></semantics></math>.
It is easy to check that evaluation of polynomials on <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>
induces an isomorphism of <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}[\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}[\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}]</annotation></semantics></math>-modules</p>
<table id="S4.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(4.6)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]/(X^{p}-X,Y^{p}-Y)\cong\mathbb{F}_{p}^{\mathbb{F}_{p}^{2}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><msubsup><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi><msubsup><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></msubsup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]/(X^{p}-X,Y^{p}-Y)\cong\mathbb{F}_{p}^{\mathbb{F}_{p}^{2}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SSx1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We can thus identify <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> with
<math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{f\in\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]/(X^{p}-X,Y^{p}-Y)\;|\;f((0,0))=0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{f\in\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]/(X^{p}-X,Y^{p}-Y)\;|\;f((0,0))=0\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> be the subspace consisting of polynomial classes
of degree <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e. those that satisfy
<math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(lx,ly)=l^{d}f(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>l</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(lx,ly)=l^{d}f(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\in\mathbb{F}_{p}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\in\mathbb{F}_{p}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>. Note that the degree is naturally
defined modulo <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p-1</annotation></semantics></math>. It is clear that the natural <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}</annotation></semantics></math>-action respects the degree.
We remark that the dimension of any <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{d}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p+1</annotation></semantics></math>.
By collecting monomials we obtain</p>
<table id="S4.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(4.7)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})=\bigoplus_{d=0}^{p-2}U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">⨁</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})=\bigoplus_{d=0}^{p-2}U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SSx1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Furthermore, we dispose of the perfect bilinear pairing</p>
<table id="S4.Ex28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})\times\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})\to\mathbb{F}_{p},\;\;\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{(a,b)\in\mathbb{F}_{p}^{2}}f(a,b)g(a,b)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.727em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></munder><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})\times\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})\to\mathbb{F}_{p},\;\;\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{(a,b)\in\mathbb{F}_{p}^{2}}f(a,b)g(a,b).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SSx1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">It is elementary to check that <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> pairs to zero
with <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{e}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{e}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> if <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(p-1)\nmid(d+e)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∤</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(p-1)\nmid(d+e)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Hence, the restricted pairing <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\times U_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\to\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\times U_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\to\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>
is perfect for <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\leq d\leq p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\leq d\leq p-1</annotation></semantics></math>,
as the dimensions of <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> are equal.
Furthermore, <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]_{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]_{d}</annotation></semantics></math> pairs to zero with <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]_{p-1-d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}[X,Y]_{p-1-d}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Consequently the induced pairing
<math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})/V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\times V_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\to\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})/V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\times V_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\to\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>
is perfect.
Composing with the map from Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm3" title="Proposition 2.3 ‣ The module 𝑉_𝑛⁢(𝑅) ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>, we obtain an isomorphism
<math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})/V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\to V_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})/V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\to V_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 4.1</span></span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S4.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> be a prime and <math id="S4.Thmthm1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> and integer with <math id="S4.Thmthm1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\leq d\leq p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\leq d\leq p-1</annotation></semantics></math>.
The preceding construction gives the exact sequence</span></p>
<table id="S4.Ex29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\to V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\to U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\to V_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\to 0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\to V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\to U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\to V_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\to 0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>

</table>
<p id="S4.Thmthm1.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmthm1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">commutes for all <math id="S4.Thmthm1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\in\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Mat</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\in\mathrm{Mat}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})_{\neq 0}</annotation></semantics></math> whose reduction modulo <math id="S4.Thmthm1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is invertible.
If <math id="S4.Thmthm1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, then the diagram is also commutative
for <math id="S4.Thmthm1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M={\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;0\\
0&amp;p\end{smallmatrix}\right)}^{\iota}=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&amp;0\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">p</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>ι</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">p</mi></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M={\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;0\\
0&amp;p\end{smallmatrix}\right)}^{\iota}=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&amp;0\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, which means in particular
that the right hand side vertical arrow is zero.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SSx1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>Only the commutativity need be checked. If <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is invertible modulo <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>,
one immediately sees that the pairing on <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> is invariant under <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>,
i.e. <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle Mf,Mg\rangle=\langle f,g\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle Mf,Mg\rangle=\langle f,g\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> for
all <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f,g\in\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f,g\in\mathcal{W}(p,\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>.
The commutativity is then clear from Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm3" title="Proposition 2.3 ‣ The module 𝑉_𝑛⁢(𝑅) ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>.
In order to treat <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&amp;0\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">p</mi></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&amp;0\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> one considers the
basis of <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> given by the monomials of degree <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, which correspond to
the embedding of <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>, together with the monomials
<math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X^{i}Y^{p-1+d-i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X^{i}Y^{p-1+d-i}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\leq i\leq p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\leq i\leq p-1</annotation></semantics></math>.
As the latter monomials all contain at least one factor of <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> by assumption,
they are killed by applying the matrix.
∎</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SSx2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Reduction to weight <math id="S4.SSx2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="S4.SSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce the following notation. Let <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be any <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-vector space
on which the Hecke operators <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> and the <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-part of the diamond operators <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle\cdot\rangle_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle\cdot\rangle_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> act.
Suppose <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
By <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M[d]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M[d]</annotation></semantics></math> we mean <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> with the action of the Hecke operator <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> “twisted”
to be <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l^{d}T_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>l</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l^{d}T_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> (in particular <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> acts as zero).
Furthermore, by <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M(d)</annotation></semantics></math> we denote the subspace
on which <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle l\rangle_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle l\rangle_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> acts as <math id="S4.SSx2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>l</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The non-parabolic part of the following proposition is also
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>, Theorem 3.4.</p>
</div>

</div>
<div id="S4.SSx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SSx2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>The first statement follows from Propositions <a href="#S3.Thmthm4" title="Proposition 3.4 ‣ Hecke operators and Shapiro’s lemma ‣ 3 Hecke action ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a> and <a href="#S3.Thmthm5" title="Proposition 3.5 ‣ Hecke operators and Shapiro’s lemma ‣ 3 Hecke action ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a>
together with the definition of <math id="S4.SSx2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>.
The first exact sequence is part of the long exact sequence
associated to the short exact sequence of Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmthm1" title="Proposition 4.1 ‣ Decomposition of 𝒲(𝑝,𝔽_𝑝) as 𝔽_𝑝⁢[Mat_2⁢(ℤ)_{≠0}]-module ‣ 4 Reduction to weight 2 for parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>.
The commutative diagram in that proposition
gives the twisting of the Hecke action in the exact sequences.
This follows directly from the description of the Hecke operator
on group cohomology.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SSx2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="S4.SSx2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=p-1</annotation></semantics></math> we have <math id="S4.SSx2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{p-1}(\mathbb{F}_{p})=V_{0}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\oplus V_{p-1}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{p-1}(\mathbb{F}_{p})=V_{0}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\oplus V_{p-1}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>,
from which the statements follow. So we now assume <math id="S4.SSx2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d&lt;p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d&lt;p-1</annotation></semantics></math>,
in particular <math id="S4.SSx2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\neq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\neq 2</annotation></semantics></math>.
For the top sequence we only need to check that it is exact on the left
and on the right. By Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm5" title="Proposition 2.5 ‣ The module 𝑉_𝑛⁢(𝑅) ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a> we have
<math id="S4.SSx2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{0}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{0}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
The <math id="S4.SSx2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>-terms are trivial by Corollary <a href="#S2.Thmthm1" title="Corollary 2.1 ‣ Cohomology of PSL_2⁢(ℤ) ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
