with <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Hence, <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{c}=g\langle T\rangle g^{-1}\cap\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>∩</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{c}=g\langle T\rangle g^{-1}\cap\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>. This
group is infinite cyclic generated by
<math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;r\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)g^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd><mtd><mi mathsize="0.700em">r</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn mathsize="0.700em">1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&amp;r\\
0&amp;1\end{smallmatrix}\right)g^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\in\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\in\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> dividing <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> (see also the proof
of Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm6" title="Proposition 2.6 ‣ Torsion-freeness and base change properties ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.6</span></a>).
Hence, we have <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{2}(D_{c},V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{2}(D_{c},V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))=0</annotation></semantics></math>.

<p id="S4.SSx2.p5.5" class="ltx_p">is exact. Lemma <a href="#S2.Thmthm4" title="Lemma 2.4 ‣ The module 𝑉_𝑛⁢(𝑅) ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.4</span></a> implies
that <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{0}(D_{c},V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{0}(D_{c},V_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{0}(D_{c},V_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{0}(D_{c},V_{p-1-d}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))</annotation></semantics></math> are
one-dimensional.
In order to finish the proof, it thus suffices to prove that <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{0}(D_{c},U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{0}(D_{c},U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))</annotation></semantics></math>
is (at least) of dimension <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>. The elements <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X^{d}\in U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X^{d}\in U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y^{d}(1-X^{p-1})\in U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y^{d}(1-X^{p-1})\in U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> are invariant under <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>. Indeed,</p>
<table id="S4.SSx2.p5.6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo </table>
<p id="S4.SSx2.p5.7" class="ltx_p">as in <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{d}(\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> we have <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X^{i}(1-X^{p-1})=X^{i-1}(X-X^{p})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X^{i}(1-X^{p-1})=X^{i-1}(X-X^{p})=0</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S4.SSx2.p5.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Modular forms of weight <math id="S5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> and level <math id="S5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Np" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Np</annotation></semantics></math></h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section recalls the reduction to weight <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>
for modular forms and establishes
a link between parabolic group cohomology and modular forms via
Jacobians of modular curves.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Reduction to weight <math id="S5.SSx1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> for modular forms</h3>

<div id="S5.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We recall some work of Serre as explained in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, Sections 7 and 8,
cf. also <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>, Section 6.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let us now introduce notation that is used
throughout the sequel of this article.
We consider the modular curve <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{1}(Np)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{1}(Np)</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Q}_{p}(\zeta_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ℚ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Q}_{p}(\zeta_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>
for a prime <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&gt;2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&gt;2</annotation></semantics></math> not dividing <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math>.
It has a regular stable model <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> over the ring <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]</annotation></semantics></math>, see
e.g. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite>.
Let <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math> denote the Néron model over <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{1}(Np)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{1}(Np)</annotation></semantics></math>,
the Jacobian of <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{1}(Np)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{1}(Np)</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Q}_{p}(\zeta_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ℚ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Q}_{p}(\zeta_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>.
We let, following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, Section 8,</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.Ex33.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=H^{0}(X,\Omega_{X/\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=H^{0}(X,\Omega_{X/\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SSx1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega_{X/\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega_{X/\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]}</annotation></semantics></math> is the <span id="S5.SSx1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">dualising sheaf of <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math></span>
of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>, Section I.2. By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, Equation 8.2, we have
for the special fibre <math id="S5.SSx1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>X</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math> that</p>
<table id="S5.Ex34" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.Ex34.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{L}}:=H^{0}(X_{\mathbb{F}_{p}},\Omega_{X_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}/\mathbb{F}_{p}})=L\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]}\mathbb{F}_{p}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{L}}:=H^{0}(X_{\mathbb{F}_{p}},\Omega_{X_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}/\mathbb{F}_{p}})=L\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]}\mathbb{F}_{p}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</div>
<div id="S5.SSx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SSx1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">On <math id="S5.SSx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SSx1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{L}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{L}}</annotation></semantics></math> the <math id="S5.SSx1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-part <math id="S5.SSx1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle\cdot\rangle_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle\cdot\rangle_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>
of the diamond operator acts.
The principal result on <math id="S5.SSx1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{L}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{L}}</annotation></semantics></math> that we will need is the following
(see Propositions 8.13 and 8.18 of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>). The
notation is as in Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 4.2 ‣ Reduction to weight 2 ‣ 4 Reduction to weight 2 for parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 5.1</span></span><span id="S5.Thmthm1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Serre)</h6>
<div id="S5.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Assume <math id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\leq k\leq p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\leq k\leq p</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then there is an isomorphism of <math id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-vector spaces</span></p>
<table id="S5.Ex35" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

</table>
<p id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">respecting the Hecke operators. Moreover, the sequence of Hecke modules</span></p>

<p id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">is exact.</span></p>

</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SSx2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Parabolic cohomology and the <math id="S5.SSx2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-torsion of the Jacobian</h3>

<div id="S5.SSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In order to compare Hecke algebras of cusp forms with
those of parabolic group cohomology in characteristic <math id="S5.SSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>, we generalise the
strategy of the second part of the proof of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, Theorem 5.2.
Hence, we wish to bring the Jacobian into the play, since it will enable us
to pass from characteristic zero geometry to characteristic <math id="S5.SSx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.Thmthm2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.Thmthm2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 5.2</span></span></h6>
<div id="S5.Thmthm2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There are isomorphisms</span></p>
<table id="S5.Ex37" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.Ex37.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{L}}\cong\mathrm{Cot}_{0}(J^{0}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}})\cong\mathrm{Cot}_{0}(J^{0}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}[p])" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Cot</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Cot</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{L}}\cong\mathrm{Cot}_{0}(J^{0}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}})\cong\mathrm{Cot}_{0}(J^{0}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}[p])</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">respecting the Hecke operators.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.SSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SSx2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>The first isomorphism is e.g. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>, Equation 6.7.2.
The second one follows from the fact that multiplication by <math id="S5.SSx2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> on
<math id="S5.SSx2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mn>0</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math> induces multiplication by <math id="S5.SSx2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> on the tangent space at <math id="S5.SSx2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>,
which is the zero map. Hence, the tangent space at <math id="S5.SSx2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S5.SSx2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}^{0}[p]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}^{0}[p]</annotation></semantics></math>
is equal to the one of <math id="S5.SSx2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mn>0</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SSx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SSx2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To establish an explicit link between parabolic cohomology and modular forms,
we identify the parabolic cohomology group for <math id="S5.SSx2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> with
<math id="S5.SSx2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-coefficients as the <math id="S5.SSx2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-torsion of the Jacobian of the corresponding
modular curve. Here we may view the Jacobian as a complex abelian variety.
As in the other cases, the Hecke correspondences on the modular curves
give rise to Hecke operators on the Jacobian.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.Thmthm3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.Thmthm3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 5.3</span></span></h6>
<div id="S5.Thmthm3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.Thmthm3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmthm3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S5.Thmthm3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math> be an integer, and <math id="S5.Thmthm3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> a prime. Then there are
isomorphisms of <math id="S5.Thmthm3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-vector spaces</span></p>
<table id="S5.Ex38" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.Ex38.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})\cong J(\mathbb{C})[p]=J({\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}})[p]" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ℚ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})\cong J(\mathbb{C})[p]=J({\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}})[p]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.Thmthm3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmthm3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">respecting the Hecke operators.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.SSx2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SSx2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SSx2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>The second equality follows from the fact that torsion points are algebraic.
We start with the exact <span id="S5.SSx2.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Kummer sequence</span> of analytic sheaves on <math id="S5.SSx2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{1}(Np)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{1}(Np)</annotation></semantics></math></p>
<table id="S5.Ex39" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.Ex39.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\to\mu_{p}\to\mathbb{G}_{m}\xrightarrow{p}\mathbb{G}_{m}\to 0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>𝔾</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝑝</mo></mover><msub><mi>𝔾</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\to\mu_{p}\to\mathbb{G}_{m}\xrightarrow{p}\mathbb{G}_{m}\to 0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S5.SSx2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Its long exact sequence in analytic cohomology yields</p>

</table>
<p id="S5.SSx2.p4.3" class="ltx_p">Using <math id="S5.SSx2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(X_{1}(Np),\mathbb{G}_{m})\cong\mathrm{Pic}_{X_{1}(Np)}(\mathbb{C})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔾</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Pic</mi><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(X_{1}(Np),\mathbb{G}_{m})\cong\mathrm{Pic}_{X_{1}(Np)}(\mathbb{C})</annotation></semantics></math>
one obtains that <math id="S5.SSx2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(X_{1}(Np),\mu_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(X_{1}(Np),\mu_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to <math id="S5.SSx2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J(\mathbb{C})[p]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(\mathbb{C})[p]</annotation></semantics></math>.
As <math id="S5.SSx2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℂ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}</annotation></semantics></math> contains the <math id="S5.SSx2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-th roots of unity, we may replace
the sheaf <math id="S5.SSx2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> by the constant sheaf <math id="S5.SSx2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Moreover, the group <math id="S5.SSx2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(X_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(X_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> coincides with
<math id="S5.SSx2.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>. This follows for example
from the Leray spectral sequence for the open immersion
<math id="S5.SSx2.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{1}(Np)\hookrightarrow X_{1}(Np)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{1}(Np)\hookrightarrow X_{1}(Np)</annotation></semantics></math> (see e.g. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>).
Since the Hecke operators come from correspondences on modular curves,
the isomorphisms are compatible for the Hecke action.
∎</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Hecke algebras</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section we compare the Hecke algebra of cuspidal modular forms
to that of parabolic group cohomology and establish isomorphisms in certain
cases. The principal result is Theorem <a href="#S6.Thmthm7" title="Theorem 6.7 ‣ Comparing Hecke algebras over 𝔽_𝑝 ‣ 6 Hecke algebras ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.7</span></a>, from which
the application to ordinary cusp forms (Corollary <a href="#S6.Thmthm9" title="Corollary 6.9 ‣ Comparing Hecke algebras over 𝔽_𝑝 ‣ 6 Hecke algebras ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.9</span></a>)
mentioned in the introduction follows.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Whenever for a ring <math id="S6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> we have an <math id="S6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>-module <math id="S6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, on which Hecke operators <math id="S6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>
act for all <math id="S6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>, we let</p>
<table id="S6.Ex41" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex41.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{R}(M):=R[T_{n}\;|\;n\in\mathbb{N}]\subseteq{\rm End}_{R}(M)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo fence="false" rspace="0.447em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊆</mo><mrow><msub><mi>End</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{R}(M):=R[T_{n}\;|\;n\in\mathbb{N}]\subseteq{\rm End}_{R}(M),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.p2.2" class="ltx_p">i.e. the <math id="S6.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>-subalgebra of the endomorphism algebra generated by
the Hecke operators.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We claim that in the situation of Hecke operators on modular forms
or group cohomology for <math id="S6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> of weight <math id="S6.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> the diamond
operators are in <math id="S6.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{R}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{R}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="S6.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> coprime to <math id="S6.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>,
let <math id="S6.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l_{1},l_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l_{1},l_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> be distinct primes which are congruent to <math id="S6.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S6.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then <math id="S6.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l_{i}^{k-1}\langle a\rangle=T^{2}_{l_{i}}-T_{l_{i}^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>l</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><msub><mi>l</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><msubsup><mi>l</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l_{i}^{k-1}\langle a\rangle=T^{2}_{l_{i}}-T_{l_{i}^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>, so
that with <math id="S6.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1=rl_{1}^{k-1}+sl_{2}^{k-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>l</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1=rl_{1}^{k-1}+sl_{2}^{k-1}</annotation></semantics></math> the claim follows.</p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">The Hecke algebra of modular forms and Eichler-Shimura</h3>

<div id="S6.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We start by stating the Eichler-Shimura theorem
(see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>, Theorem 12.2.2 and Proposition 12.4.10).</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_thm">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 6.1</span></span><span id="S6.Thmthm1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Eichler-Shimura)</h6>
<div id="S6.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="S6.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.Thmthm1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\leq\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>SL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\leq\mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> a congruence subgroup
there is an isomorphism of <math id="S6.Thmthm1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{Z}}(S_{k}(\Gamma,\mathbb{C}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>ℤ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{Z}}(S_{k}(\Gamma,\mathbb{C}))</annotation></semantics></math>-modules,
the Eichler-Shimura isomorphism,</span></p>
<table id="S6.Ex42" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex42.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}(\mathbb{C}))\cong S_{k}(\Gamma,\mathbb{C})\oplus\overline{S_{k}(\Gamma,\mathbb{C})}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}(\mathbb{C}))\cong S_{k}(\Gamma,\mathbb{C})\oplus\overline{S_{k}(\Gamma,\mathbb{C})}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S6.Thmthm2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.Thmthm2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 6.2</span></span></h6>
<div id="S6.Thmthm2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.Thmthm2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.Thmthm2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="S6.Thmthm2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.Thmthm2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math> we have natural ring isomorphisms</span></p>
<table id="S6.Ex43" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex43.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{Z}}\big(S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C})\big)\cong\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{Z}}\big(H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(\mathbb{Z}))/\mathrm{torsion}\big)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>ℤ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>ℤ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>torsion</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{Z}}\big(S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C})\big)\cong\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{Z}}\big(H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(\mathbb{Z}))/\mathrm{torsion}\big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S6.SSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SSx1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>The free <math id="S6.SSx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>-module
<math id="S6.SSx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(\mathbb{Z}))/\mathrm{torsion}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>torsion</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(\mathbb{Z}))/\mathrm{torsion}</annotation></semantics></math>
is a <math id="S6.SSx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>-structure in the <math id="S6.SSx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℂ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}</annotation></semantics></math>-vector space <math id="S6.SSx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(\mathbb{C}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(\mathbb{C}))</annotation></semantics></math>.
Any <math id="S6.SSx1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>-structure gives an isomorphic Hecke algebra.
Finally, Theorem <a href="#S6.Thmthm1" title="Theorem 6.1 (Eichler-Shimura) ‣ The Hecke algebra of modular forms and Eichler-Shimura ‣ 6 Hecke algebras ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a> implies that
the Hecke algebra of <math id="S6.SSx1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(\mathbb{C}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(\mathbb{C}))</annotation></semantics></math>
is isomorphic to the Hecke algebra of <math id="S6.SSx1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{C})</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SSx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SSx1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The formula in this corollary is the reason why many people prefer
to factor out the torsion of modular symbols.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.Thmthm3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.Thmthm3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 6.3</span></span></h6>
<div id="S6.Thmthm3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.Thmthm3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.Thmthm3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S6.Thmthm3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.Thmthm3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math> integers and <math id="S6.Thmthm3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math> a prime.
Then we have</span></p>

</div>
</div>
<div id="S6.SSx1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SSx1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SSx1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>, Theorem 12.3.2,
there is no difference between Katz cusp forms over <math id="S6.SSx1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>
and those that are reductions of classical cusp forms
whose <math id="S6.SSx1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>-expansion is in <math id="S6.SSx1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}[1/N]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}[1/N]</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e.</p>

<p id="S6.SSx1.p4.4" class="ltx_p">Tensoring the first one with <math id="S6.SSx1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> allows us to compare it to the
second one, from which the proposition follows.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.Thmthm4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.Thmthm4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 6.4</span></span></h6>
<div id="S6.Thmthm4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.Thmthm4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.Thmthm4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S6.Thmthm4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> be a prime and <math id="S6.Thmthm4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.Thmthm4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\leq k\leq p+2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\leq k\leq p+2</annotation></semantics></math> integers s.t. <math id="S6.Thmthm4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then sending the operator <math id="S6.Thmthm4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S6.Thmthm4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> for all primes <math id="S6.Thmthm4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>
defines a surjective <math id="S6.Thmthm4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-algebra homomorphism</span></p>
<table id="S6.Ex48" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="S6.SSx1.p5.4" class="ltx_p">is compatible with Hecke operators, and allows one to define a homomorphism
from the Hecke algebra on the left hand term to the one on the

of the Hecke algebra.

<div id="S6.Thmthm5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.Thmthm5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 6.5</span></span></h6>
<div id="S6.Thmthm5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math> be integers and <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> a field.
If the characteristic of <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, then we assume <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math>.
Furthermore, let <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon:\Gamma_{0}(N)\overset{\mathrm{proj}}{\twoheadrightarrow}\Gamma_{0}(N)/\Gamma_{1}(N)\to K^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mo stretchy="false">↠</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">proj</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon:\Gamma_{0}(N)\overset{\mathrm{proj}}{\twoheadrightarrow}\Gamma_{0}(N)/\Gamma_{1}(N)\to K^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>
be a character such that <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon(-1)=(-1)^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon(-1)=(-1)^{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Denote by <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝕋</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}</annotation></semantics></math> the <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>-Hecke algebra of <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),K)</annotation></semantics></math> and by
<math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> the <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>-Hecke algebra of <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,K)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Furthermore, let</span></p>
<table id="S6.Ex52" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex52.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I=(\langle\delta\rangle-\epsilon(\delta)\;|\;\delta\in\Gamma_{0}(N)/\Gamma_{1}(N))\lhd\mathbb{T}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊲</mo><mi>𝕋</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I=(\langle\delta\rangle-\epsilon(\delta)\;|\;\delta\in\Gamma_{0}(N)/\Gamma_{1}(N))\lhd\mathbb{T}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Then <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}/I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝕋</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}/I</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> are isomorphic <math id="S6.Thmthm5.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>-algebras.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S6.SSx1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SSx1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SSx1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>As we work with Katz modular cusp forms (for that we need the condition <math id="S6.SSx1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math>),
we dispose of the <math id="S6.SSx1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>-expansion principle. Hence we have
isomorphisms respecting the Hecke action
<math id="S6.SSx1.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbb{T}_{\epsilon})^{\vee}\cong S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,K)\cong\mathbb{T}^{\vee}[I]\cong(\mathbb{T}/I)^{\vee}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∨</mo></msup><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝕋</mi><mo>∨</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>I</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝕋</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∨</mo></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbb{T}_{\epsilon})^{\vee}\cong S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,K)\cong\mathbb{T}^{\vee}[I]\cong(\mathbb{T}/I)^{\vee},</annotation></semantics></math>
whence the proposition follows.
∎</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SSx2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Comparing Hecke algebras over <math id="S6.SSx2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="S6.Thmthm6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.Thmthm6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 6.6</span></span></h6>
<div id="S6.Thmthm6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.Thmthm6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.Thmthm6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S6.Thmthm6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math> be an integer, <math id="S6.Thmthm6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math> a prime and <math id="S6.Thmthm6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\leq d\leq p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\leq d\leq p-1</annotation></semantics></math> an integer.
There exists a surjection
<math id="S6.Thmthm6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\big(H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})(d)\big)\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}({\overline{L}}(d))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↠</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\big(H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})(d)\big)\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}({\overline{L}}(d))</annotation></semantics></math>
such that the diagram of <math id="S6.Thmthm6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-algebras</span></p>

<p id="S6.Thmthm6.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.Thmthm6.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">commutes. All maps are uniquely determined by sending the Hecke operator <math id="S6.Thmthm6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S6.Thmthm6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}</annotation></semantics></math>
for all primes l.</span></p>
