<div id="S6.SSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SSx2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>Let us first remark how the diagonal arrows are made. The lower one comes
from the isomorphism (see Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm6" title="Proposition 2.6 ‣ Torsion-freeness and base change properties ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.6</span></a>)</p>
<table id="S6.Ex54" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex54.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{Z})\otimes\mathbb{F}_{p}\cong H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{Z})\otimes\mathbb{F}_{p}\cong H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SSx2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The upper one is due to the fact that <math id="S6.SSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> is a lattice in
<math id="S6.SSx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{2}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{Q}_{p}(\zeta_{p}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ℚ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{2}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{Q}_{p}(\zeta_{p}))</annotation></semantics></math> (see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, p. 472) and
using arguments as in Corollary <a href="#S6.Thmthm2" title="Corollary 6.2 ‣ The Hecke algebra of modular forms and Eichler-Shimura ‣ 6 Hecke algebras ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.2</span></a>.
As the order of <math id="S6.SSx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> is invertible in <math id="S6.SSx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, we can everywhere
pass to the eigencomponents of the action of the <math id="S6.SSx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-part of the diamond
operator <math id="S6.SSx2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle\cdot\rangle_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle\cdot\rangle_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We obtain the vertical arrow by showing that the kernel of the lower diagonal
map is contained in the kernel of the upper diagonal map. In other words,
we will show that if a Hecke operator <math id="S6.SSx2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> in
<math id="S6.SSx2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{Z}}\big(S_{2}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{C})(d)\big)\otimes\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>ℤ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.055em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{Z}}\big(S_{2}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{C})(d)\big)\otimes\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>
acts as zero on <math id="S6.SSx2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})(d)</annotation></semantics></math>, then it acts as zero on
<math id="S6.SSx2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{L}}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{L}}(d)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SSx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SSx2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">So assume that <math id="S6.SSx2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> acts as zero on <math id="S6.SSx2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{F}_{p})(d)</annotation></semantics></math>.
By Proposition <a href="#S5.Thmthm3" title="Proposition 5.3 ‣ Parabolic cohomology and the 𝑝-torsion of the Jacobian ‣ 5 Modular forms of weight 2 and level 𝑁⁢𝑝 ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>, it acts as zero on <math id="S6.SSx2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}}({\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}})[p](d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ℚ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ℚ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}}({\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}})[p](d)</annotation></semantics></math>,
hence on <math id="S6.SSx2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}}[p](d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ℚ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{p}}}[p](d)</annotation></semantics></math>, as <math id="S6.SSx2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}}[p]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>ℚ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}}[p]</annotation></semantics></math> is reduced.
But then it also acts as zero on <math id="S6.SSx2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]}[p](d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mrow><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]}[p](d)</annotation></semantics></math>, as it acts as
zero on the generic fibre
using that <math id="S6.SSx2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J[p]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J[p]</annotation></semantics></math> is flat over <math id="S6.SSx2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}_{p}[\zeta_{p}]</annotation></semantics></math> (<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>, Lemma 7.3.2,
as <math id="S6.SSx2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math> is semi-abelian).
But consequently, it also acts as zero on
the special fibre <math id="S6.SSx2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}[p](d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}[p](d)</annotation></semantics></math>, whence also on the cotangent space
<math id="S6.SSx2.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Cot}_{0}(J_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}^{0}[p])(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Cot</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Cot}_{0}(J_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}^{0}[p])(d)</annotation></semantics></math>. Now Lemma <a href="#S5.Thmthm2" title="Lemma 5.2 ‣ Parabolic cohomology and the 𝑝-torsion of the Jacobian ‣ 5 Modular forms of weight 2 and level 𝑁⁢𝑝 ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a> finishes the proof.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.Thmthm7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_thm">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.Thmthm7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 6.7</span></span></h6>
<div id="S6.Thmthm7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.Thmthm7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.Thmthm7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S6.Thmthm7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> be a prime and <math id="S6.Thmthm7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2&lt;k\leq p+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2&lt;k\leq p+1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.Thmthm7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math> integers such that <math id="S6.Thmthm7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math>.
We write for short
<math id="S6.Thmthm7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}^{\mathrm{par},N,k}:=\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\big(H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝕋</mi><mrow><mi>par</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}^{\mathrm{par},N,k}:=\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\big(H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))\big)</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S6.Thmthm7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}^{\mathrm{mod},N,k}:=\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\big(S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝕋</mi><mrow><mi>mod</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}^{\mathrm{mod},N,k}:=\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\big(S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})\big)</annotation></semantics></math> and
similarly for the twisted ones.
Then there is the commutative diagram of <math id="S6.Thmthm7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-algebras</span></p>
<table id="S6.Ex55" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="S6.Thmthm7.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.Thmthm7.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The vertical arrows are obtained from Proposition <a href="#S6.Thmthm6" title="Proposition 6.6 ‣ Comparing Hecke algebras over 𝔽_𝑝 ‣ 6 Hecke algebras ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.6</span></a>
resp. Corollary <a href="#S6.Thmthm4" title="Corollary 6.4 ‣ The Hecke algebra of modular forms and Eichler-Shimura ‣ 6 Hecke algebras ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.4</span></a>, and the horizontal
ones from Proposition <a href="#S5.Thmthm1" title="Proposition 5.1 (Serre) ‣ Reduction to weight 2 for modular forms ‣ 5 Modular forms of weight 2 and level 𝑁⁢𝑝 ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a> and Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 4.2 ‣ Reduction to weight 2 ‣ 4 Reduction to weight 2 for parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>.
The vertical arrows are surjective.
If <math id="S6.Thmthm7.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2&lt;k\leq p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2&lt;k\leq p</annotation></semantics></math>, then the upper horizontal arrow is injective.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S6.SSx2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SSx2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SSx2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>The commutativity is clear, as <math id="S6.SSx2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> is sent to <math id="S6.SSx2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}\times T_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}\times T_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> along the horizontal
arrows, and <math id="S6.SSx2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> is sent to <math id="S6.SSx2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> along the vertical arrows for all primes <math id="S6.SSx2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>.
The surjectivity of the vertical arrows has been proved at the places
cited above.
The injectivity of the upper homomorphism is the fact that <math id="S6.SSx2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{L}}(k-2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{L}}(k-2)</annotation></semantics></math>
is the direct sum of <math id="S6.SSx2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SSx2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{p+3-k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})[k-2]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{p+3-k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})[k-2]</annotation></semantics></math>,
if <math id="S6.SSx2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2&lt;k\leq p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2&lt;k\leq p</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.Thmthm8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.Thmthm8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 6.8</span></span></h6>
<div id="S6.Thmthm8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.Thmthm8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.Thmthm8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S6.Thmthm8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2&lt;k\leq p+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2&lt;k\leq p+1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.Thmthm8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S6.Thmthm8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="S6.Thmthm8.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔓</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{P}</annotation></semantics></math> be a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra
<math id="S6.Thmthm8.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{Z}}\big(S_{2}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{C})(d)\big)\otimes\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>ℤ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.055em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{Z}}\big(S_{2}(\Gamma_{1}(Np),\mathbb{C})(d)\big)\otimes\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>
which is not in the support of <math id="S6.Thmthm8.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{p+3-k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{p+3-k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then we have an isomorphism</span></p>

</div>
<div id="S6.SSx2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SSx2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SSx2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>The assumption means that <math id="S6.SSx2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(S_{p+3-k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})[k-2])_{\mathfrak{P}}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝔓</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(S_{p+3-k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})[k-2])_{\mathfrak{P}}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
By Corollary <a href="#S6.Thmthm4" title="Corollary 6.4 ‣ The Hecke algebra of modular forms and Eichler-Shimura ‣ 6 Hecke algebras ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.4</span></a> the ideal <math id="S6.SSx2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔓</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{P}</annotation></semantics></math> is not in the
support of <math id="S6.SSx2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{p+1-k}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))[k-2]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{p+1-k}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))[k-2]</annotation></semantics></math> either, whence
<math id="S6.SSx2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{p+1-k}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))[k-2])_{\mathfrak{P}}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝔓</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{p+1-k}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))[k-2])_{\mathfrak{P}}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Hence, the sequences of Propositions <a href="#S4.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 4.2 ‣ Reduction to weight 2 ‣ 4 Reduction to weight 2 for parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> and <a href="#S5.Thmthm1" title="Proposition 5.1 (Serre) ‣ Reduction to weight 2 for modular forms ‣ 5 Modular forms of weight 2 and level 𝑁⁢𝑝 ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>
localised at <math id="S6.SSx2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔓</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{P}</annotation></semantics></math> give isomorphisms
<math id="S6.SSx2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\big({\overline{L}}(k-2)\big)_{\mathfrak{P}}\cong\mathbb{T}^{\mathrm{mod},N,k}_{\mathfrak{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝔓</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≅</mo><msubsup><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>𝔓</mi><mrow><mi>mod</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\big({\overline{L}}(k-2)\big)_{\mathfrak{P}}\cong\mathbb{T}^{\mathrm{mod},N,k}_{\mathfrak{P}}</annotation></semantics></math>
and
<math id="S6.SSx2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}^{\mathrm{par},Np,2}_{\mathfrak{P}}\cong\mathbb{T}^{\mathrm{par},N,k}_{\mathfrak{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>𝔓</mi><mrow><mi>par</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>≅</mo><msubsup><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>𝔓</mi><mrow><mi>par</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}^{\mathrm{par},Np,2}_{\mathfrak{P}}\cong\mathbb{T}^{\mathrm{par},N,k}_{\mathfrak{P}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Hence, also the vertical maps in the localisation at <math id="S6.SSx2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔓</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{P}</annotation></semantics></math> of the diagram
of Theorem <a href="#S6.Thmthm7" title="Theorem 6.7 ‣ Comparing Hecke algebras over 𝔽_𝑝 ‣ 6 Hecke algebras ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.7</span></a> are isomorphisms.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.Thmthm9" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.Thmthm9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 6.9</span></span></h6>
<div id="S6.Thmthm9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.Thmthm9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.Thmthm9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S6.Thmthm9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2&lt;k\leq p+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2&lt;k\leq p+1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.Thmthm9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S6.Thmthm9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="S6.Thmthm9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔓</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{P}</annotation></semantics></math> be a maximal ideal of <math id="S6.Thmthm9.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\big(S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\big(S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})\big)</annotation></semantics></math>
corresponding to a normalised eigenform <math id="S6.Thmthm9.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f\in S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f\in S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}})</annotation></semantics></math>
which is ordinary, i.e. <math id="S6.Thmthm9.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{p}(f)\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{p}(f)\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then we have an isomorphism</span></p>
<table id="S6.Ex57" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

</div>
<div id="S6.SSx2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SSx2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SSx2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>As the operator <math id="S6.SSx2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> always acts as zero on <math id="S6.SSx2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{p+3-k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})[k-2]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{p+3-k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})[k-2]</annotation></semantics></math>
the maximal ideal <math id="S6.SSx2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔓</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{P}</annotation></semantics></math> cannot be in the support of <math id="S6.SSx2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{p+3-k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})[k-2]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{p+3-k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})[k-2]</annotation></semantics></math>,
whence we are in the situation of Corollary <a href="#S6.Thmthm8" title="Corollary 6.8 ‣ Comparing Hecke algebras over 𝔽_𝑝 ‣ 6 Hecke algebras ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.8</span></a>.
∎</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Application to <math id="S7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{0}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{0}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> and characters</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The techniques from the preceding sections do not apply to the group
<math id="S7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{0}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{0}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>. In this section we show that one can, nevertheless,
derive similar results for that group together with a
character of the quotient group <math id="S7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{0}(N)/\Gamma_{1}(N)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{0}(N)/\Gamma_{1}(N)\cong(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let us for the sequel of this section make the following assumption.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_ass">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S7.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Assumption 7.1</span></span></h6>
<div id="S7.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math> be a prime and <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> a finite field of characteristic <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>
or <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K={\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K={\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Suppose, moreover, that we are given integers <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>
with <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\leq k\leq p+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\leq k\leq p+1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=\Gamma_{0}(N)/\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=\Gamma_{0}(N)/\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>.
It acts on <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>, the parabolic subspace and on
<math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),K)</annotation></semantics></math> through the diamond operators.
Furthermore, let <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> be a character of the form
<math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon:\Gamma_{0}(N)\overset{\mathrm{proj}}{\twoheadrightarrow}\Gamma_{0}(N)/\Gamma_{1}(N)\to K^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mo stretchy="false">↠</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">proj</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon:\Gamma_{0}(N)\overset{\mathrm{proj}}{\twoheadrightarrow}\Gamma_{0}(N)/\Gamma_{1}(N)\to K^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Denote by <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K^{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K^{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> the <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K[\Gamma_{0}(N)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K[\Gamma_{0}(N)]</annotation></semantics></math>-module which is a copy of <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> with
action through <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We write <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{k-2}^{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{k-2}^{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> for the <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K[\Gamma_{0}(N)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K[\Gamma_{0}(N)]</annotation></semantics></math>-module
<math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{k-2}(K)\otimes_{K}K^{\epsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mi>K</mi></msub><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{k-2}(K)\otimes_{K}K^{\epsilon}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Finally, let <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> be the group with <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)\leq G\leq\Gamma_{0}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)\leq G\leq\Gamma_{0}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>
such that <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G/\Gamma_{1}(N)=\Delta_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G/\Gamma_{1}(N)=\Delta_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, the <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-Sylow subgroup of <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>.
Note that <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> acts freely on <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℍ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{H}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S7.Thmthm2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S7.Thmthm2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 7.2</span></span></h6>
<div id="S7.Thmthm2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.Thmthm2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.Thmthm2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let us assume <a href="#S7.Thmthm1" title="Assumption 7.1 ‣ 7 Application to Γ_0⁢(𝑁) and characters ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.1</span></a>. Then
<math id="S7.Thmthm2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(K))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(K))</annotation></semantics></math> and its parabolic subspace
are coinduced <math id="S7.Thmthm2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K[\Delta_{p}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K[\Delta_{p}]</annotation></semantics></math>-modules.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>We write <math id="S7.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V=V_{k-2}(K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V=V_{k-2}(K)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma:=\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma:=\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>.
The Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence (in the notation from
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>, Appendix B,
we use the exact sequence <math id="S7.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{1}^{2}\to E_{2}^{1,1}\to E_{2}^{3,0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msubsup><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msubsup><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{1}^{2}\to E_{2}^{1,1}\to E_{2}^{3,0}</annotation></semantics></math>)
gives the exact sequence</p>

<p id="S7.p3.3" class="ltx_p">whence <math id="S7.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Delta_{p},H^{1}(\Gamma,V))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Delta_{p},H^{1}(\Gamma,V))</annotation></semantics></math> is zero by
Corollary <a href="#S2.Thmthm1" title="Corollary 2.1 ‣ Cohomology of PSL_2⁢(ℤ) ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> and Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm5" title="Proposition 2.5 ‣ The module 𝑉_𝑛⁢(𝑅) ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a>.
From Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 2.2 ‣ Definition of parabolic group cohomology ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> it follows taking <math id="S7.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-cohomology
that the sequence</p>

accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">res</mo></mover><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">\</mo><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\to H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma,V)^{\Delta_{p}}\to H^{1}(\Gamma,V)^{\Delta_{p}}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}}\big(\prod_{g\in\Gamma\backslash\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})/\langle T\rangle}H^{1}(\Gamma\cap\langle gTg^{-1}\rangle,V)\big)^{\Delta_{p}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S7.Ex59"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S7.Ex59.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\to H^{1}(\Delta_{p},H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma,V))\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\to H^{1}(\Delta_{p},H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma,V))\to 0</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.p3.4" class="ltx_p">is exact. It can be checked (using that <math id="S7.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1\not\in G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>∉</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1\not\in G</annotation></semantics></math> and
that <math id="S7.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> does not divide the ramification
indices of the cusps) that the first three terms are</p>
<table id="S7.Ex60" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.Ex60.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\to H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(G,V)\to H^{1}(G,V)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}}\prod_{g\in movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">\</mo><msub><mi>PSL</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>T</mi><mo
