encoding="application/x-tex">0\to H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(G,V)\to H^{1}(G,V)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}}\prod_{g\in G\backslash\mathrm{PSL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})/\langle T\rangle}H^{1}(G\cap\langle gTg^{-1}\rangle,V)\to 0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.p3.5" class="ltx_p">where the zero on the right is again a consequence of Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 2.2 ‣ Definition of parabolic group cohomology ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>.
Hence, <math id="S7.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Delta_{p},H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma,V))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Delta_{p},H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma,V))</annotation></semantics></math> is zero.
Finally, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite>, Proposition 1.7.3(ii), implies that
<math id="S7.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Gamma,V)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Gamma,V)</annotation></semantics></math> and its parabolic subspace
are coinduced <math id="S7.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-modules.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.Thmthm3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S7.Thmthm3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 7.3</span></span></h6>
<div id="S7.Thmthm3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.Thmthm3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.Thmthm3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let us assume <a href="#S7.Thmthm1" title="Assumption 7.1 ‣ 7 Application to Γ_0⁢(𝑁) and characters ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.1</span></a>. Then <math id="S7.Thmthm3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),K)</annotation></semantics></math>
is a free <math id="S7.Thmthm3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K[\Delta_{p}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K[\Delta_{p}]</annotation></semantics></math>-module.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S7.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>For the notation in this proof we follow <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>, pp. 209-210
and the proof of Lemma 1.9. We let <math id="S7.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma:=\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma:=\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The projection
<math id="S7.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi:X_{\Gamma}\twoheadrightarrow X_{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">↠</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>G</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi:X_{\Gamma}\twoheadrightarrow X_{G}</annotation></semantics></math> is a Galois
cover with group <math id="S7.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> of projective <math id="S7.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>-schemes. Indeed, for the
open part this is <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>, VI.2.7. Moreover,
the ramification index of the cusps divides <math id="S7.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>,
whence the cusps are unramified in a <math id="S7.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-extension.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Using Serre duality and the Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism
(see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>, VI.4.5.2) we obtain</p>
<table id="S7.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S7.Ex61"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S7.Ex61.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle H^{1}(X_{G},\omega^{\otimes k}(-\mathrm{cusps}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>cusps</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle H^{1}(X_{G},\omega^{\otimes k}(-\mathrm{cusps}))</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S7.Ex61.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\overset{\text{S-D}}{\cong}H^{0}(X_{G},\Omega^{1}\otimes(\omega^{\otimes k}(-\mathrm{cusps}))^{\vee})^{\vee}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>≅</mo><mtext mathsize="0.700em">S-D</mtext></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>cusps</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∨</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∨</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\overset{\text{S-D}}{\cong}H^{0}(X_{G},\Omega^{1}\otimes(\omega^{\otimes k}(-\mathrm{cusps}))^{\vee})^{\vee}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S7.Ex62"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S7.Ex62.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\overset{\text{K-S}}{\cong}H^{0}(X_{G},\omega^{\otimes 2-k})^{\vee}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>≅</mo><mtext mathsize="0.700em">K-S</mtext></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∨</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\overset{\text{K-S}}{\cong}H^{0}(X_{G},\omega^{\otimes 2-k})^{\vee}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.p6.2" class="ltx_p">which is zero, since the degree of <math id="S7.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega^{\otimes 2-k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega^{\otimes 2-k}</annotation></semantics></math> is negative (as <math id="S7.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math>).
The map <math id="S7.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> is étale and we have
<math id="S7.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{0}(X_{\Gamma},\pi^{*}\omega^{\otimes k}(-\mathrm{cusps}))\cong S_{k}(\Gamma,K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>π</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>cusps</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{0}(X_{\Gamma},\pi^{*}\omega^{\otimes k}(-\mathrm{cusps}))\cong S_{k}(\Gamma,K)</annotation></semantics></math>.
We conclude from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite>, Theorem 2, that this is a
free <math id="S7.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K[\Delta_{p}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K[\Delta_{p}]</annotation></semantics></math>-module.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.Thmthm4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_thm">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S7.Thmthm4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 7.4</span></span></h6>
<div id="S7.Thmthm4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.Thmthm4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.Thmthm4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let us assume <a href="#S7.Thmthm1" title="Assumption 7.1 ‣ 7 Application to Γ_0⁢(𝑁) and characters ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.1</span></a> and that
<math id="S7.Thmthm4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(K))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{k-2}(K))</annotation></semantics></math> is a faithful <math id="S7.Thmthm4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{K}(S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),K))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{K}(S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),K))</annotation></semantics></math>-module.
Then <math id="S7.Thmthm4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{0}(N),V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{0}(N),V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})</annotation></semantics></math> is a faithful
module for <math id="S7.Thmthm4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}_{K}(S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,K))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝕋</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}_{K}(S_{k}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,K))</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S7.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>Let <math id="S7.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma:=\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma:=\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>.
We claim that <math id="S7.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\Delta}:=\sum_{\delta\in\Delta}\delta\in K[\Delta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">:=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow></msub><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\Delta}:=\sum_{\delta\in\Delta}\delta\in K[\Delta]</annotation></semantics></math>
induces isomorphisms</p>

<p id="S7.p7.3" class="ltx_p">We note that <math id="S7.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}(K))\otimes_{K}K^{\epsilon}=H^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mi>K</mi></msub><msup><mi>K</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}(K))\otimes_{K}K^{\epsilon}=H^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})</annotation></semantics></math>,
since the character <math id="S7.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> restricted to <math id="S7.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> is trivial.
Using Lemmas <a href="#S7.Thmthm2" title="Lemma 7.2 ‣ 7 Application to Γ_0⁢(𝑁) and characters ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.2</span></a> and <a href="#S7.Thmthm3" title="Lemma 7.3 ‣ 7 Application to Γ_0⁢(𝑁) and characters ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.3</span></a>,
an elementary calculation gives the claim.</p>
</div>

<p id="S7.p8.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S7.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math> is the ideal defined in Proposition <a href="#S6.Thmthm5" title="Proposition 6.5 ‣ The Hecke algebra of modular forms and Eichler-Shimura ‣ 6 Hecke algebras ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.5</span></a>. In view of that
proposition, we only need to show that if <math id="S7.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> acts as zero on <math id="S7.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(G,V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(G,V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})</annotation></semantics></math>,
then <math id="S7.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> is in <math id="S7.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p9.1" class="ltx_p">The Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence yields
<math id="S7.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})^{\Delta}\cong H^{1}(G,V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></msup></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})^{\Delta}\cong H^{1}(G,V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})</annotation></semantics></math>,
since <math id="S7.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})^{\Gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})^{\Gamma}</annotation></semantics></math> is zero by Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm5" title="Proposition 2.5 ‣ The module 𝑉_𝑛⁢(𝑅) ‣ 2 Parabolic group cohomology ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a>.
Let now <math id="S7.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> be a Hecke operator. Then we have</p>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S7.Ex64.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=T\cdot H^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})^{\Delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=T\cdot H^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})^{\Delta}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S7.Ex65"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S7.Ex65.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=TN_{\Delta}\cdot H^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})_{\Delta}=T(\sum_{\delta\in\Delta}\epsilon(\delta)^{-1}\langle\delta\rangle)\cdot H^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}(K))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=TN_{\Delta}\cdot H^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}^{\epsilon})_{\Delta}=T(\sum_{\delta\in\Delta}\epsilon(\delta)^{-1}\langle\delta\rangle)\cdot H^{1}(\Gamma,V_{k-2}(K))</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.p9.2" class="ltx_p">Suppose that this is zero. Hence, by the assumed faithfulness we have that
<math id="S7.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T(\sum_{\delta\in\Delta}\epsilon(\delta)^{-1}\langle\delta\rangle)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T(\sum_{\delta\in\Delta}\epsilon(\delta)^{-1}\langle\delta\rangle)=0</annotation></semantics></math>,
which by Equation (<a href="#S7.E10" title="In 7 Application to Γ_0⁢(𝑁) and characters ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.10</span></a>) implies <math id="S7.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\in I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\in I</annotation></semantics></math>, as required.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.Thmthm5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_rem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S7.Thmthm5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 7.5</span></span></h6>
<div id="S7.Thmthm5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.Thmthm5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.Thmthm5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If <math id="S7.Thmthm5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=2</annotation></semantics></math>, then the statements of Theorem <a href="#S7.Thmthm4" title="Theorem 7.4 ‣ 7 Application to Γ_0⁢(𝑁) and characters ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.4</span></a> also hold
“outside the Eisenstein part”. The Eisenstein part is the subspace
on which the Hecke algebra acts via a system of eigenvalues that does not
belong to an irreducible Galois representation.
For, a suitable analogue of Lemma <a href="#S7.Thmthm3" title="Lemma 7.3 ‣ 7 Application to Γ_0⁢(𝑁) and characters ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.3</span></a> holds, since
<math id="S7.Thmthm5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{1}(X_{G},\omega^{\otimes k}(-\mathrm{cusps}))\cong H^{0}(X_{G},\mathcal{O})^{\vee}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>cusps</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∨</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{1}(X_{G},\omega^{\otimes k}(-\mathrm{cusps}))\cong H^{0}(X_{G},\mathcal{O})^{\vee}</annotation></semantics></math>
cannot give rise to a non-Eisenstein system of eigenvalues.
Moreover, under the extra assumption
also Lemma <a href="#S7.Thmthm2" title="Lemma 7.2 ‣ 7 Application to Γ_0⁢(𝑁) and characters ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.2</span></a> remains valid, as an easy calculation
shows.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">8 </span>Application to weight one modular forms</h2>

<div id="S8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Edixhoven explains in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, Section 4, how weight one cuspidal
Katz modular forms over finite fields of characteristic <math id="S8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> can be computed from the
knowledge of the Hecke algebra of weight <math id="S8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> cusp forms over the same field.
In this section we shall first recall this and then derive the conclusion
mentioned in the introduction that weight one modular cusp forms over <math id="S8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}}</annotation></semantics></math>
can be computed by the Hecke operators on weight <math id="S8.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> parabolic group
cohomology over <math id="S8.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S8.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔽</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}</annotation></semantics></math> be a finite field of prime characteristic <math id="S8.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S8.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}}</annotation></semantics></math> and
fix a level <math id="S8.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S8.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math> and a character
<math id="S8.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon:(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{*}\to\mathbb{F}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>𝔽</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon:(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{*}\to\mathbb{F}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S8.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon(-1)=(-1)^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon(-1)=(-1)^{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We have two injections of <math id="S8.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔽</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}</annotation></semantics></math>-vector spaces</p>
<table id="S8.Ex66" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S8.Ex66.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F,A:S_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})\to S_{p}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F,A:S_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})\to S_{p}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S8.p2.2" class="ltx_p">given on <math id="S8.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>-expansions by <math id="S8.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{n}(Ag)=a_{n}(g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{n}(Ag)=a_{n}(g)</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S8.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{n}(Fg)=a_{n/p}(g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{n}(Fg)=a_{n/p}(g)</annotation></semantics></math> (with <math id="S8.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{n}(Fg)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{n}(Fg)=0</annotation></semantics></math> if <math id="S8.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid n</annotation></semantics></math>),
which are compatible with all Hecke operators <math id="S8.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> for primes <math id="S8.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\neq p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\neq p</annotation></semantics></math>.
The former comes from the <span id="S8.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Frobenius</span> and the latter is multiplication
by the <span id="S8.p2.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Hasse invariant</span>.
One has <math id="S8.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{p}^{(p)}F=A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{p}^{(p)}F=A</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S8.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AT_{p}^{(1)}=T_{p}^{(p)}A+\epsilon(p)F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AT_{p}^{(1)}=T_{p}^{(p)}A+\epsilon(p)F</annotation></semantics></math>, where we have indicated the
weight as a superscript (see e.g. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, Equation (4.1.2)).</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S8.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}^{(k)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝕋</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}^{(k)}</annotation></semantics></math> be the Hecke algebra over <math id="S8.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔽</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}</annotation></semantics></math>
of weight <math id="S8.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> for a fixed level <math id="S8.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> and a fixed character <math id="S8.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>.
We will also indicate the weight of Hecke operators by superscripts.
We denote by <math id="S8.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math> the <math id="S8.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>-subalgebra of <math id="S8.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝕋</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math>
generated by all Hecke operators <math id="S8.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{n}^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{n}^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S8.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid n</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 8.1</span></span></h6>
<div id="S8.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S8.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S8.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(a)</span> 
<div id="S8.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There is a homomorphism </span><math id="S8.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, called a derivation,
which on </span><math id="S8.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-expansions is given by
</span><math id="S8.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{n}(\Theta f)=na_{n}(f)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{n}(\Theta f)=na_{n}(f)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> such that the sequence</span></p>

<p id="S8.I1.i1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I1.i1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">is exact.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S8.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(b)</span> 
<div id="S8.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Suppose </span><math id="S8.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f\in S_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f\in S_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> such that </span><math id="S8.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{n}(f)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{n}(f)=0</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> for
all </span><math id="S8.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> with </span><math id="S8.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid n</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">. Then </span><math id="S8.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f=0</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.
In particular </span><math id="S8.I1.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AS_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})\cap FS_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∩</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AS_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})\cap FS_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})=0</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S8.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(c)</span> 
<div id="S8.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The Hecke algebra </span><math id="S8.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}^{(1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝕋</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}^{(1)}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> in weight one can be generated by
all </span><math id="S8.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}^{(1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}^{(1)}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, where </span><math id="S8.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> runs through the primes different from </span><math id="S8.I1.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S8.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(d)</span> 
<div id="S8.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The weight one Hecke algebra </span><math id="S8.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}^{(1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝕋</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}^{(1)}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> is the algebra generated
by the </span><math id="S8.I1.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-action on the module </span><math id="S8.I1.i4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}^{(p)}/A^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝕋</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}^{(p)}/A^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I1.i4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>(a) The main theorem of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite> gives the exact sequence</p>
<table id="S8.Ex68" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S8.Ex68.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\to S_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})\xrightarrow{F}S_{p}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})\xrightarrow{A\Theta}S_{2p+1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝐹</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.700em">A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.700em" mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi></mrow></mover><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\to S_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})\xrightarrow{F}S_{p}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})\xrightarrow{A\Theta}S_{2p+1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S8.p4.2" class="ltx_p">by taking Galois invariants.
However, as explained in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, Section 4,
the image <math id="S8.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A\Theta S_{p}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A\Theta S_{p}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})</annotation></semantics></math> in weight <math id="S8.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2p+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2p+1</annotation></semantics></math> can be
divided by the Hasse invariant, whence the weight is as claimed.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p5.1" class="ltx_p">(b) The condition implies by looking
at <math id="S8.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>-expansions that <math id="S8.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A\Theta f=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A\Theta f=0</annotation></semantics></math>, whence by Part (3) of Katz’ theorem
cited above <math id="S8.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> comes from a lower weight than <math id="S8.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, but below there is just the
<math id="S8.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>-form (see also <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, Proposition 4.4).</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p6.1" class="ltx_p">(c) It is enough to show that <math id="S8.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{p}^{(1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{p}^{(1)}</annotation></semantics></math> is linearly dependent on the span of all
<math id="S8.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{n}^{(1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{n}^{(1)}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S8.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid n</annotation></semantics></math>. If it were not, then there would be a modular cusp form
of weight <math id="S8.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying <math id="S8.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{n}(f)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{n}(f)=0</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S8.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid n</annotation></semantics></math>,
but <math id="S8.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{p}(f)\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{p}(f)\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math>, contradicting (b).</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p7.1" class="ltx_p">(d) Dualising the exact sequence in (a) yields that <math id="S8.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}^{(p)}/A^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝕋</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}^{(p)}/A^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}^{(1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝕋</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}^{(1)}</annotation></semantics></math>
are isomorphic as <math id="S8.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math>-modules, which implies the claim.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.Thmthm2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.Thmthm2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 8.2</span></span></h6>
<div id="S8.Thmthm2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math> be integers such that <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid N</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}|\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔽</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}|\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> a finite extension
and let <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon:(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{*}\to\mathbb{F}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>𝔽</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon:(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{*}\to\mathbb{F}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> be a character with <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon(-1)=(-1)^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon(-1)=(-1)^{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Set</span></p>

<p id="S8.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Then the Hecke operators
</span><math id="S8.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{1}^{(k)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{1}^{(k)}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I2.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, </span><math id="S8.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{2}^{(k)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{2}^{(k)}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I2.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, </span><math id="S8.I2.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dots" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dots</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I2.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, </span><math id="S8.I2.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{kB}^{(k)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{kB}^{(k)}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I2.i1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">
generate </span><math id="S8.I2.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{T}^{(k)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝕋</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{T}^{(k)}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I2.i1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> as an </span><math id="S8.I2.i1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔽</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I2.i1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-vector space.</span></p>
</div></li>

can already be generated as an </span><math id="S8.I2.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔽</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I2.i2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-vector space by the set</span></p>

<div id="S8.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>(a) This follows from the proof of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, Proposition 4.2.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p9.1" class="ltx_p">(b) Assume that some
<math id="S8.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{m}^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{m}^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S8.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m&gt;(p+2)B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m&gt;(p+2)B</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid m</annotation></semantics></math> is linearly independent of the
operators in the set of the assertion. This means that there
is a cusp form <math id="S8.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f\in S_{p}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f\in S_{p}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})</annotation></semantics></math>
satisfying <math id="S8.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{n}(f)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{n}(f)=0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S8.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\leq(p+2)B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\leq(p+2)B</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S8.p9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\nmid n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\nmid n</annotation></semantics></math>, but <math id="S8.p9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m}(f)\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m}(f)\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
One gets <math id="S8.p9.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{n}(\Theta f)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{n}(\Theta f)=0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S8.p9.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\leq(p+2)B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\leq(p+2)B</annotation></semantics></math>, but
<math id="S8.p9.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{m}(\Theta f)\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{m}(\Theta f)\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math>. This contradicts (a).
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.Thmthm3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_rem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.Thmthm3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 8.3</span></span></h6>
<div id="S8.Thmthm3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If we work with <math id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> and no character, the number <math id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> above
has to be replaced by</span></p>
