<div id="S8.Thmthm4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.Thmthm4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 8.4</span></span></h6>
<div id="S8.Thmthm4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.Thmthm4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.Thmthm4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V\subset S_{p}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,{\overline{\mathbb{F}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V\subset S_{p}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,{\overline{\mathbb{F}}})</annotation></semantics></math> be the eigenspace of a
system of eigenvalues for the operators <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math> for all primes <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\neq p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\neq p</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
<div id="S8.Thmthm4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If the system of eigenvalues does not come from a weight one form,
then <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> is at most of dimension one.
Conversely, if there is a normalised weight one eigenform <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>
with that system of eigenvalues
for <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}^{(1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}^{(1)}</annotation></semantics></math> for all primes <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\neq p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\neq p</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V=\langle Ag,Fg\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V=\langle Ag,Fg\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> and that
space is <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional.
On it <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{p}^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{p}^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math> acts with eigenvalues <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon(p)u^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon(p)u^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>
satisfying <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u+\epsilon(p)u^{-1}=a_{p}(g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u+\epsilon(p)u^{-1}=a_{p}(g)</annotation></semantics></math>.
In particular, the eigenforms in weight <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> which come from weight one are ordinary.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>We choose a normalised eigenform <math id="S8.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> for all operators.
If <math id="S8.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> is at least <math id="S8.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional, then we have
<math id="S8.p11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V=\mathbb{F}f\oplus\{h\;|\;a_{n}(h)=0\;\forall p\nmid n\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔽</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>|</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.447em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∤</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V=\mathbb{F}f\oplus\{h\;|\;a_{n}(h)=0\;\forall p\nmid n\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
As a form <math id="S8.p11.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> in the right summand is annihilated by <math id="S8.p11.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta</annotation></semantics></math>, it is
equal to <math id="S8.p11.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Fg" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Fg</annotation></semantics></math> for some form <math id="S8.p11.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> of weight one by Proposition <a href="#S8.Thmthm1" title="Proposition 8.1 ‣ 8 Application to weight one modular forms ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.1</span></a> (a).
By Part (b) of that proposition we know that <math id="S8.p11.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle Ag,Fg\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle Ag,Fg\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>
is <math id="S8.p11.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional. If <math id="S8.p11.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> were more than <math id="S8.p11.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional, then there
would be two different cusp forms in weight <math id="S8.p11.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, which are eigenforms for all <math id="S8.p11.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{l}^{(1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{l}^{(1)}</annotation></semantics></math>
with <math id="S8.p11.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\neq p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\neq p</annotation></semantics></math>. This, however, contradicts Part (c).</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p12.1" class="ltx_p">Assume now that <math id="S8.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S8.p12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional.
Any normalised eigenform <math id="S8.p12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f\in V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f\in V</annotation></semantics></math> for all Hecke operators in weight <math id="S8.p12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>
has to be of the form <math id="S8.p12.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Ag+\mu Fg" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Ag+\mu Fg</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="S8.p12.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu\in{\overline{\mathbb{F}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu\in{\overline{\mathbb{F}}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The eigenvalue of <math id="S8.p12.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{p}^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{p}^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S8.p12.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is the <math id="S8.p12.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-th coefficient,
hence <math id="S8.p12.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u=a_{p}(g)+\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u=a_{p}(g)+\mu</annotation></semantics></math>, as <math id="S8.p12.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{p}(Fg)=a_{1}(g)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{p}(Fg)=a_{1}(g)=1</annotation></semantics></math>.
Now we have</p>
<table id="S8.EGx4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S8.Ex72"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S8.Ex72.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=T_{p}^{(p)}(Ag+\mu Fg)=T_{p}^{(p)}Ag+\mu Ag" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=T_{p}^{(p)}(Ag+\mu Fg)=T_{p}^{(p)}Ag+\mu Ag</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S8.Ex73"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S8.Ex73.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=AT_{p}^{(1)}g-\epsilon(p)Fg+\mu Ag=(a_{p}(g)+\mu)Ag-\epsilon(p)Fg," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=AT_{p}^{(1)}g-\epsilon(p)Fg+\mu Ag=(a_{p}(g)+\mu)Ag-\epsilon(p)Fg,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S8.p12.2" class="ltx_p">which implies <math id="S8.p12.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-\epsilon(p)=(a_{p}(g)+\mu)\mu=u^{2}-ua_{p}(g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\epsilon(p)=(a_{p}(g)+\mu)\mu=u^{2}-ua_{p}(g)</annotation></semantics></math>
by looking at the <math id="S8.p12.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>-th coefficient. From this one obtains the claim on <math id="S8.p12.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.Thmthm5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_thm">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.Thmthm5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 8.5</span></span></h6>
<div id="S8.Thmthm5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.Thmthm5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.Thmthm5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S8.Thmthm5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math> an integer and <math id="S8.Thmthm5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> be a prime not dividing <math id="S8.Thmthm5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S8.Thmthm5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S8.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S8.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(a)</span> 
<div id="S8.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The Hecke algebra of
</span><math id="S8.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I3.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> can be computed using
the first </span><math id="S8.I3.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(p+2)B^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(p+2)B^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I3.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> Hecke operators on </span><math id="S8.I3.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{p-2}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),V_{p-2}(\mathbb{F}_{p}))</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I3.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S8.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(b)</span> 
<div id="S8.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let </span><math id="S8.I3.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝔽</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I3.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> be a finite field of characteristic </span><math id="S8.I3.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I3.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">
and let </span><math id="S8.I3.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon:(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{*}\to\mathbb{F}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>𝔽</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon:(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{*}\to\mathbb{F}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I3.i2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> be a character.
The Hecke algebra of </span><math id="S8.I3.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\epsilon,\mathbb{F})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I3.i2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> can be computed using
the first </span><math id="S8.I3.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(p+2)B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(p+2)B</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I3.i2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> Hecke operators on </span><math id="S8.I3.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{0}(N),V_{p-2}^{\epsilon}(\mathbb{F}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝔽</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{0}(N),V_{p-2}^{\epsilon}(\mathbb{F}))</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S8.I3.i2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="S8.Thmthm5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.Thmthm5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The numbers <math id="S8.Thmthm5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> resp. <math id="S8.Thmthm5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> were defined in Proposition <a href="#S8.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 8.2 ‣ 8 Application to weight one modular forms ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.2</span></a>
and Remark <a href="#S8.Thmthm3" title="Remark 8.3 ‣ 8 Application to weight one modular forms ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.3</span></a>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.p13" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p13.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.p13.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span>(a) Corollary <a href="#S6.Thmthm9" title="Corollary 6.9 ‣ Comparing Hecke algebras over 𝔽_𝑝 ‣ 6 Hecke algebras ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.9</span></a> implies that the ordinary part of <math id="S8.p13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>
is a faithful module for the ordinary part of the Hecke algebra of weight <math id="S8.p13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> Katz cusp
forms over <math id="S8.p13.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{F}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{F}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>. So that part of the Hecke algebra can be computed using
the Hecke operators <math id="S8.p13.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{1},\dots,T_{pB^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{1},\dots,T_{pB^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S8.p13.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>par</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝔽</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\mathrm{par}}^{1}(\Gamma_{1}(N),\mathbb{F}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> (see Proposition <a href="#S8.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 8.2 ‣ 8 Application to weight one modular forms ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.2</span></a>(a)).
From Proposition <a href="#S8.Thmthm4" title="Proposition 8.4 ‣ 8 Application to weight one modular forms ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.4</span></a> we know that the image of the weight one
forms in weight <math id="S8.p13.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> under the Hasse invariant and Frobenius lies in the ordinary part.
Proposition <a href="#S8.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 8.2 ‣ 8 Application to weight one modular forms ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.2</span></a>(b) implies that <math id="S8.p13.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math> can be computed by the
Hecke operators indicated there.
Now the Hecke algebra of weight one Katz cusp forms on <math id="S8.p13.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{1}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{1}(N)</annotation></semantics></math> without
a character can be computed as described in Proposition <a href="#S8.Thmthm1" title="Proposition 8.1 ‣ 8 Application to weight one modular forms ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.1</span></a>(d).</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p14" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p14.1" class="ltx_p">(b) Under the extra assumption and using Theorem <a href="#S7.Thmthm4" title="Theorem 7.4 ‣ 7 Application to Γ_0⁢(𝑁) and characters ‣ On the faithfulness of parabolic cohomologyas a Hecke module over a finite field" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.4</span></a>,
the same arguments also work with a character and the bound <math id="S8.p14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</p>
</div>
</section>

<span id="bib.bib18.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Etale cohomology</span>. Princeton Mathematical Series, <span id="bib.bib18.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">33</span>.
Princeton University Press, Princeton, N.J., 1980.

</span></li>
      
<li id="bib.bib19" class="ltx_bibitem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_bibitem">[19]</span>
<span class="ltx_bibblock"> S. Nakajima.

of an algebraic variety</span>. Inv. math. <span id="bib.bib19.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">75</span> (1984), 1–8.

</span></li>
      
<li id="bib.bib20" class="ltx_bibitem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_bibitem">[20]</span>
<span class="ltx_bibblock"> J. Neukirch, A. Schmidt and K. Wingberg.
<span id="bib.bib20.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Cohomology of Number Fields</span>,
Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften <span id="bib.bib20.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">323</span>, Springer, Berlin, 2000.

</span></li>
      
<li id="bib.bib21" class="ltx_bibitem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_bibitem">[21]</span>

Princeton University Press, 1994.

</span></li>
      
<li id="bib.bib22" class="ltx_bibitem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_bibitem">[22]</span>
<span class="ltx_bibblock"> G. Wiese. <span id="bib.bib22.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Computing Hecke algebras of weight <math id="bib.bib22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> in Magma.</span>
Appendix B of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>.

</span></li>
